title: The Yellow School Bus
p: In the United States, many children go to school by bus.
在美国，很多孩子坐校车上学。
The buses are big and bright yellow.
校车又大又是鲜艳的黄色。
Drivers can see the color easily, even in the rain or early in the morning.
即使在雨天或清晨，司机们也能很容易看到这种颜色。
When the bus stops, a red sign comes out from its side.
校车停下时，车身侧面会伸出一块红色的牌子。
The sign says STOP.
牌子上写着“STOP（停）”。
In most places, cars on both sides of the road must stop and wait.
在大多数地方，道路两侧的汽车都必须停下等待。
This way, children can cross the road safely.
这样，孩子们就能安全地过马路。
q: What color are most school buses in the U.S.?
What comes out from the side of the bus?
So children can cross the road safely
So the bus can turn around
ph: Katy Warner from Orlando, FL, USA

title: Sunday Roast
p: In Britain, many families eat a big meal on Sunday.
在英国，很多家庭会在周日吃一顿丰盛的饭。
It is called a Sunday roast.
这顿饭叫作“周日烤肉”。
The meat is usually beef, chicken, lamb or pork.
肉通常是牛肉、鸡肉、羊肉或猪肉。
The meat comes with roast potatoes and vegetables, like carrots and peas.
肉会配上烤土豆和蔬菜，比如胡萝卜和豌豆。
With beef, people often eat Yorkshire pudding.
吃牛肉时，人们常常配约克郡布丁。
It is not a sweet pudding — it is a light, puffy food made from eggs, flour and milk.
它不是甜布丁，而是一种用鸡蛋、面粉和牛奶做成的轻盈蓬松的食物。
Last, everyone pours hot gravy over their plate.
最后，大家把热乎乎的肉汁浇在自己的盘子上。
q: When do many British families eat a roast?
What is Yorkshire pudding made from?
What do people pour over their food?

title: Trick or Treat!
p: Halloween is on October 31st.
万圣节是 10 月 31 日。
Before the day, people buy big orange pumpkins.
节日前，人们会买又大又橙的南瓜。
They cut faces into them and put a light inside.
他们在南瓜上刻出脸，在里面放一盏灯。
These are called jack-o'-lanterns.
这叫作南瓜灯。
In the evening, children wear costumes.
晚上，孩子们穿上装扮服。
Some are witches, ghosts or superheroes.
有的扮成女巫、幽灵或超级英雄。
They knock on doors and say, "Trick or treat!"
他们去敲门，说：“不给糖就捣蛋！”
Neighbors give them candy, and the children say thank you.
邻居们给他们糖果，孩子们说谢谢。
q: A pumpkin with a face and a light inside
What do children say at the door?

title: The Yard Sale
p: On sunny Saturday mornings in America, you may see a sign that says "Yard Sale."
在美国，阳光明媚的周六早上，你可能会看到写着“Yard Sale（院子拍卖）”的牌子。
A family puts old things on tables in front of their house.
一家人把旧东西摆在自家门前的桌子上。
There are books, toys, lamps, clothes and sometimes even bikes.
有书、玩具、台灯、衣服，有时甚至还有自行车。
Everything is cheap, and buyers often ask for a lower price.
东西都很便宜，买的人还常常讲价。
This is normal, and the seller usually says yes with a smile.
这很正常，卖家通常会笑着答应。
The family gets a cleaner house, and the buyers go home with something "new."
这家人的房子变整洁了，买的人也带着“新”东西回家。
q: Where are the things at a yard sale?
On tables in front of a house

title: Fish and Chips
p: Fish and chips is a famous meal in Britain.
炸鱼薯条是英国很有名的一道餐。
The fish is often cod or haddock, cooked in a light batter.
鱼通常是鳕鱼或黑线鳕，裹上一层薄面糊炸。
The chips are thick potato fries.
薯条是粗粗的炸土豆条。
People buy it at a "chippy," a small fish and chip shop.
人们在“chippy”——一种卖炸鱼薯条的小店里买。
They add salt and vinegar on top.
他们会在上面撒盐、洒醋。
Some people also like mushy peas, which are soft green peas.
有些人还喜欢豌豆泥，就是软软的绿豌豆。
On a summer day by the sea, many people eat it outside.
夏天在海边，很多人会在户外吃。
q: What do people put on fish and chips?

title: A Day with a Mail Carrier
p: Maria is a mail carrier in a small town in Ohio.
玛丽亚是俄亥俄州一个小镇的邮递员。
She starts work at seven in the morning at the post office.
她早上七点在邮局开始工作。
First, she puts the letters and packages in order.
首先，她把信件和包裹按顺序整理好。
Then she drives her white mail truck around town.
然后她开着白色的邮车在镇上转。
She puts letters in mailboxes and leaves packages at front doors.
她把信放进信箱，把包裹放在人家门口。
In winter it is cold, and in summer it is hot, but she likes her job.
冬天冷，夏天热，但她喜欢这份工作。
"I know every street and every dog," she says with a laugh.
“每条街、每只狗我都认识。”她笑着说。
q: She puts letters and packages in order
She rides a bike to deliver mail

title: Thanksgiving Dinner
p: Thanksgiving is a big holiday in the United States.
感恩节是美国的一个重要节日。
It is on the fourth Thursday of November.
它在十一月的第四个星期四。
Families travel far to eat dinner together.
家人们会从很远的地方赶回来一起吃晚饭。
The main dish is a large roast turkey.
主菜是一只大大的烤火鸡。
There are also mashed potatoes, stuffing and cranberry sauce.
还有土豆泥、填馅和蔓越莓酱。
For dessert, many people eat pumpkin pie.
甜点方面，很多人吃南瓜派。
Before the meal, some families say what they are thankful for.
饭前，有些家庭会说说自己感激的事情。
q: On the fourth Thursday of November
On the first Monday of December
What do many people eat for dessert?

title: My Library Card
p: Most towns in the US and the UK have a public library.
美国和英国的大多数城镇都有公共图书馆。
A library card is usually free for people who live in the area.
对住在当地的人来说，借书证通常是免费的。
With the card, you can borrow books, movies and music.
有了借书证，你可以借书、电影和音乐。
Libraries are not only for books.
图书馆不只是用来看书的。
You can use the computers and the Wi-Fi.
你可以使用电脑和无线网络。
There are story times for little children and clubs for adults.
有给小朋友的讲故事时间，也有给成年人的俱乐部。
On a cold day, it is a warm and quiet place to sit.
冷天里，这是一个可以坐下来的温暖又安静的地方。

title: Self-Checkout
p: In many supermarkets today, you can pay without a cashier.
如今在很多超市，你不用收银员就能付款。
You go to a self-checkout machine.
你去自助结账机那里。
You scan each item, put it in your bag, and pay by card or phone.
你扫描每件商品，放进袋子，然后用卡或手机付款。
Some people love it because it is fast.
有些人很喜欢，因为速度快。
Other people don't like it.
也有人不喜欢。
Sometimes the machine says, "Unexpected item in the bagging area!"
有时机器会说：“装袋区有意外物品！”
Then a worker has to come and help.
这时就得有店员过来帮忙。
q: What do you do first at self-checkout?
Give your bag to a worker
Why do some people like self-checkout?
It is open only at night
What happens when the machine has a problem?
You get the food for free

title: The Lifeguard
p: Jack is a lifeguard at a beach in California.
杰克是加州一处海滩的救生员。
He sits in a tall wooden tower and watches the water.
他坐在一座高高的木制瞭望台上，看着海面。
He has a red rescue float and a whistle.
他有一个红色的救生浮具和一只哨子。
If a swimmer is in trouble, he runs into the sea fast.
如果有游泳的人遇到危险，他会飞快地冲进海里。
But most of the day, he answers questions and tells people where it is safe to swim.
但一天里的大部分时间，他在回答问题，告诉人们哪里游泳比较安全。
He has to be a strong swimmer and know first aid.
他必须游泳技术好，还要懂急救。
"The best day," he says, "is a day when nobody needs me."
“最好的一天，”他说，“就是没有人需要我的一天。”
q: What does Jack do most of the day?
Answers questions and gives safety advice
A day when nobody needs help
A day when he rescues many people

title: To Tip or Not to Tip
p: For many visitors, tipping is one of the most confusing parts of American life.
对许多游客来说，给小费是美国生活中最让人困惑的事情之一。
In restaurants with table service, leaving a tip is not required by law, but it is strongly expected.
在有服务员送餐的餐厅里，法律并不要求给小费，但人们普遍认为应该给。
Many servers rely on tips for a large part of their income, so leaving nothing is seen as rude.
很多服务员收入的很大一部分靠小费，所以一分不给会被认为很失礼。
Tips are usually calculated as a percentage of the bill before tax.
小费通常按税前账单金额的一定比例来计算。
People also commonly tip taxi drivers, hairdressers and hotel staff who carry their bags.
人们通常也会给出租车司机、理发师和帮忙搬行李的酒店员工小费。
In Britain, the custom is much more relaxed.
在英国，这一习俗要随意得多。
Some restaurants add a service charge to the bill, and if they don't, a tip of around ten percent is a polite but optional gesture.
有些餐厅会在账单里加收服务费；如果没有，给一成左右的小费是一种礼貌但可有可无的表示。
So before you pay, it is always worth checking the bill carefully.
所以付钱之前，最好仔细看一下账单。
q: Why is leaving no tip seen as rude in American restaurants?
Servers rely on tips for much of their income
The manager keeps all the money
How are tips usually calculated in the US?
As a percentage of the bill
As a fixed amount per person
What does the article suggest doing in Britain?
Check whether a service charge is already on the bill
Tip only the chef, in cash

title: The Story of Afternoon Tea
p: Afternoon tea is often linked with Anna, the seventh Duchess of Bedford, in the 1840s.
下午茶常被认为与 19 世纪 40 年代的第七代贝德福德公爵夫人安娜有关。
At that time, wealthy people ate dinner late in the evening, and she felt hungry in the afternoon.
当时有钱人晚饭吃得很晚，她到下午就饿了。
She began asking for tea and a light snack around four o'clock, and soon she was inviting friends to join her.
她开始在四点左右要茶和小点心，不久便邀请朋友一起享用。
Today, a traditional afternoon tea is served on a tiered stand.
如今，传统的下午茶用多层点心架端上来。
Small sandwiches, such as cucumber or egg, are on the bottom; scones are in the middle; and cakes and pastries are on top.
黄瓜或鸡蛋等小三明治放在最下层，司康饼在中间，蛋糕和酥点在最上层。
Scones are eaten with clotted cream and jam, but people argue about which should go on first.
司康要配凝脂奶油和果酱，但先抹哪一样，人们争论不休。
In Devon, cream traditionally goes first, while in Cornwall, it is jam first.
在德文郡，传统上先抹奶油；而在康沃尔，则是先抹果酱。
Few British people have afternoon tea every day, but it remains a popular treat for birthdays and special occasions.
很少有英国人每天都喝下午茶，但它仍然是过生日和特殊场合时很受欢迎的享受。
q: Why did the Duchess start having afternoon tea?
She felt hungry because dinner was served late
Her doctor told her to drink more tea
Tea had just arrived in Britain

What is the tradition in Cornwall?

Scones are eaten with butter only

title: Remember, Remember the Fifth of November
p: On the evening of November 5th, the skies over Britain fill with fireworks.
11 月 5 日晚上，英国的夜空中满是烟花。
This is Bonfire Night, also known as Guy Fawkes Night.
这就是篝火之夜，也叫盖伊·福克斯之夜。
It remembers an event from 1605 called the Gunpowder Plot.
它纪念的是 1605 年一起被称为“火药阴谋”的事件。
A group of men planned to blow up the Houses of Parliament in London and kill King James I.
一伙人计划炸毁伦敦的议会大厦，并杀死国王詹姆斯一世。
Guy Fawkes was caught guarding barrels of gunpowder in a cellar under the building.
盖伊·福克斯在大楼下的地窖里看守成桶的火药时被抓获。
The plot failed, and people lit bonfires to celebrate that the king was safe.
阴谋失败了，人们点起篝火庆祝国王平安无事。
Today, towns hold large public firework displays, and some people still burn a model of Guy Fawkes, called a "guy," on the fire.
如今，各地会举办大型公共烟花表演，有些人仍会把一个叫“guy”的盖伊·福克斯人偶放到火里烧掉。
Families stand in the cold, eating toffee apples and waving sparklers.
一家人站在寒风中，吃着太妃糖苹果，挥舞着手持烟花棒。
q: What did the plotters want to do?
Blow up Parliament and kill the king
Why did people first light bonfires on this day?
To celebrate that the king was safe
What is a "guy" in this article?
A model of Guy Fawkes burned on the fire

title: Behind the Coffee Bar
p: Emma has worked as a barista in a busy Seattle café for three years.
艾玛在西雅图一家繁忙的咖啡馆做了三年咖啡师。
Her shift begins at 5:30 a.m., before the doors open, when she cleans the espresso machine and tests the first shots of coffee.
她的班早上 5 点半开始，那时还没开门，她要清洁意式咖啡机，并试萃第一批咖啡。
"If the first shot tastes bitter, I adjust the grind," she explains.
“如果第一杯尝起来发苦，我就调整研磨粗细。”她解释说。
Between seven and nine, the line rarely stops.
七点到九点之间，排队的人几乎没有断过。
Office workers order lattes with oat milk, extra-hot cappuccinos and drinks with long, complicated names.
上班族点燕麦奶拿铁、特别烫的卡布奇诺，还有名字又长又复杂的饮品。
Emma has to remember several orders at once while chatting with regular customers.
艾玛得同时记住好几份订单，还要跟熟客聊天。
The hardest part is not the coffee but staying calm and friendly under pressure.
最难的不是咖啡本身，而是在压力下保持冷静和友好。
Still, she loves the moment when a tired customer takes the first sip and smiles.
不过，她很喜欢疲惫的顾客喝下第一口后露出笑容的那一刻。
q: What does Emma do if the first shot tastes bitter?
Staying calm and friendly under pressure

title: Working from the Kitchen Table
p: Since 2020, millions of office workers in Britain and the United States have spent at least part of the week working from home.
2020 年以来，英美数以百万计的上班族每周至少有一部分时间在家办公。
For many, the change began suddenly during the COVID-19 pandemic, but it did not disappear afterward.
对许多人来说，这一变化是在新冠疫情期间突然开始的，但疫情过后它并没有消失。
Supporters say remote work saves hours of commuting and gives parents more flexibility.
支持者说，远程办公省下了好几个小时的通勤时间，也让父母们更加灵活。
Video calls, shared online documents and chat apps let teams work together from different cities.
视频通话、在线共享文档和聊天应用让团队成员身处不同城市也能协作。
However, some people feel lonely, and others find it hard to stop working when the office is also the living room.
然而，有些人感到孤独，还有些人发现，当办公室同时也是客厅时，很难停下工作。
As a result, many companies now use a "hybrid" model, in which employees come into the office two or three days a week.
因此，许多公司现在采用“混合”模式，员工每周到办公室两三天。
The debate about where work should happen is likely to continue for years.
关于应该在哪里工作的争论，很可能还会持续多年。

Which problem of remote work is mentioned?
Working some days at home and some in the office

title: Quiz Night at the Pub
p: Walk into a British pub on a weekday evening and you might hear someone shout, "Question number seven!"
工作日晚上走进一家英国酒吧，你可能会听到有人大喊：“第七题！”
Pub quizzes are a popular weekly tradition across the UK.
酒吧问答是全英国很受欢迎的每周传统活动。
Friends form small teams, choose a funny team name, and sit around a table with a pen and an answer sheet.
朋友们组成小队，起一个搞笑的队名，围坐在桌边，拿着笔和答题纸。
The quizmaster asks questions on general knowledge, sports, music, movies and history.
主持人会出常识、体育、音乐、电影和历史方面的题。
There is often a picture round, in which teams have to recognize famous faces.
通常还有一轮看图题，各队要认出名人的脸。
Using phones to search for answers is strictly forbidden.
用手机搜答案是严格禁止的。
The prize is usually small — perhaps a bottle of wine or a voucher for the bar — but the real reward is the fun of arguing over answers with friends.
奖品通常不大——也许是一瓶葡萄酒或一张酒吧代金券——但真正的收获是和朋友争论答案的乐趣。

title: The American Diner
p: With their shiny counters, red booths and neon signs, diners are an American icon.
闪亮的吧台、红色卡座和霓虹招牌——小餐馆（diner）是美国的标志之一。
Many of them serve breakfast all day, so you can order pancakes and bacon at ten o'clock at night.
很多小餐馆全天供应早餐，所以晚上十点你也能点煎饼和培根。
A typical menu is huge: burgers, grilled cheese sandwiches, milkshakes, meatloaf and pie.
典型的菜单很长：汉堡、烤奶酪三明治、奶昔、肉糕和馅饼。
When you order eggs, the server will ask how you want them — scrambled, sunny side up, or over easy.
你点鸡蛋时，服务员会问你想怎么做——炒蛋、单面煎，还是两面煎（蛋黄不熟）。
In many diners, your coffee cup is refilled again and again without you even asking.
在很多小餐馆里，不用你开口，咖啡杯就会被一次又一次续满。
Diners are places where truck drivers, students and families all sit side by side.
在小餐馆里，卡车司机、学生和一家老小都挨着坐。
For many Americans, they are less about fancy food and more about comfort and a friendly face.
对很多美国人来说，小餐馆的意义不在于精致的食物，而在于舒适和一张友好的面孔。

title: Pancake Day
p: In Britain, the day before Lent begins is called Shrove Tuesday, but most people know it as Pancake Day.
在英国，大斋期开始前的那一天叫“忏悔星期二”，但大多数人管它叫“煎饼日”。
Traditionally, Christians gave up rich foods like eggs, butter and sugar during the forty days of Lent.
按照传统，基督徒在四十天的大斋期里不吃鸡蛋、黄油、糖这类油腻丰盛的食物。
Making pancakes was a good way to use them up before the fast began.
做煎饼是在斋戒开始前把它们用完的好办法。
British pancakes are thin, more like French crêpes than thick American ones.
英式煎饼很薄，更像法式可丽饼，而不像厚厚的美式煎饼。
The classic topping is a squeeze of lemon juice and a sprinkle of sugar.
经典吃法是挤一点柠檬汁，再撒一点糖。
Some towns hold pancake races, in which runners must flip a pancake in a frying pan as they run.
有些城镇会举办煎饼赛跑，参赛者必须边跑边用平底锅颠煎饼。
The race in Olney, Buckinghamshire, is said to date back to 1445.
据说白金汉郡奥尔尼的煎饼赛跑可以追溯到 1445 年。
Because Lent depends on the date of Easter, Pancake Day falls on a different date every year, usually in February or early March.
由于大斋期取决于复活节的日期，煎饼日每年的日期都不同，通常在二月或三月初。

To use up rich foods before Lent
Because it was the king's birthday
To sell eggs at the market

title: The Night Nurse
p: At 7:30 p.m., when most people are going home, David starts his twelve-hour shift as a nurse in a hospital in Manchester.
晚上 7 点半，大多数人正要回家时，大卫在曼彻斯特一家医院开始了他十二小时的护士夜班。
First, he listens carefully as the day nurses explain each patient's condition.
首先，他仔细听白班护士讲解每位病人的情况。
During the night, he checks blood pressure, gives medicine on time and writes everything down in the patients' records.
夜里，他测量血压、按时给药，并把一切都记在病历上。
Some patients cannot sleep and want someone to talk to, so he often sits with them for a few minutes.
有些病人睡不着，想找人说说话，所以他常常陪他们坐几分钟。
If a patient's condition gets worse, he must act quickly and call a doctor.
如果病人情况恶化，他必须迅速行动，叫来医生。
Working nights is tiring, and David sleeps during the day with thick curtains to block out the light.
上夜班很累，大卫白天睡觉时要拉上厚窗帘挡光。
But he says the quiet hours give him a special connection with his patients.
但他说，那些安静的时光让他和病人之间有一种特别的联系。
q: What does David do at the start of his shift?
Listens to the day nurses explain each patient's condition
Why does he sometimes sit with patients?
Some cannot sleep and want to talk
He is too tired to walk
How does David sleep during the day?
With thick curtains to block the light

title: Can You Trust Online Reviews?
p: Before choosing a restaurant, a hotel or even a plumber, many people now check online reviews.
如今，在选餐厅、酒店，甚至找水管工之前，很多人都会先看网上评论。
A row of five stars can bring a small business many new customers, while a few angry comments can keep people away.
一排五星好评能给小店带来很多新顾客，而几条愤怒的评论就可能让人望而却步。
But not every review can be trusted.
但并不是每条评论都可信。
Some businesses pay for fake positive reviews, and some competitors post fake negative ones.
有些商家花钱买虚假好评，有些竞争对手则发布虚假差评。
Governments in both the UK and the US have taken steps against fake reviews.
英国和美国政府都已采取措施打击虚假评论。
Experts suggest reading several reviews, not just looking at the score.
专家建议多读几条评论，而不是只看评分。
Detailed comments that mention specific dishes or staff are usually more reliable than short ones that just say "Amazing!"
提到具体菜品或员工的详细评论，通常比只写一句“太棒了！”的简短评论更可靠。
q: Why are some reviews not trustworthy?
Who might post fake negative reviews?
Which kind of review is usually more reliable?
A detailed one that mentions specific things

title: Get Your Kicks on Route 66
p: Route 66 was one of the original highways in the US national highway system, created in 1926.
66 号公路是美国国道系统最早的公路之一，建于 1926 年。
It ran for about 2,400 miles (3,900 km) from Chicago to Santa Monica, California, crossing eight states.
它从芝加哥延伸到加州圣莫尼卡，全长约 2400 英里（3900 公里），途经八个州。
In the 1930s, families escaping the Dust Bowl drove it west in search of work, and the writer John Steinbeck called it "the Mother Road."
20 世纪 30 年代，逃离“沙尘暴重灾区”的家庭沿着这条路向西寻找工作，作家约翰·斯坦贝克称它为“母亲之路”。
After World War II, it became a symbol of freedom and family road trips, lined with motels, gas stations and diners.
二战后，它成了自由和家庭公路旅行的象征，沿途遍布汽车旅馆、加油站和小餐馆。
As faster interstate highways were built, Route 66 was officially removed from the highway system in 1985.
随着更快的州际公路建成，66 号公路于 1985 年被正式从国道系统中撤销。
Yet many sections survive, and travelers from around the world still drive them to see the old neon signs and small towns.
但许多路段保留了下来，世界各地的旅行者仍会驾车前来，看看那些老霓虹招牌和小镇。
q: Where did Route 66 start and end?
Why was Route 66 removed from the highway system?

title: Low and Slow: Southern Barbecue
zh: 慢火烟熏：美国南方烧烤
p: In the American South, "barbecue" does not simply mean grilling burgers in the backyard.
在美国南方，“barbecue”可不只是在后院烤汉堡肉饼。
It means cooking meat slowly for many hours over low heat and wood smoke, until it is tender enough to pull apart with a fork.
它指的是用小火和木柴烟熏把肉慢慢烤上好几个小时，直到肉嫩得用叉子就能撕开。
Every region is proud of its own style.
每个地区都以自己的风格为傲。
In Texas, beef brisket is king, often seasoned with little more than salt and black pepper.
在得克萨斯，牛胸肉是王者，往往只用盐和黑胡椒调味。
In the Carolinas, pork is the favorite, sometimes served with a sharp vinegar-based sauce.
在南北卡罗来纳，猪肉最受欢迎，有时配上酸味浓烈的醋基酱汁。
Kansas City is famous for its thick, sweet tomato-based sauce, while Memphis is known for ribs covered in a dry spice rub.
堪萨斯城以浓稠香甜的番茄基酱汁闻名，而孟菲斯则以抹满干香料的肋排著称。
Barbecue fans can argue for hours about which style is best — and the only way to decide is to taste them all.
烧烤迷们可以为哪种风格最好争上几个小时——而唯一的评判办法就是挨个尝一遍。
q: Slowly over low heat and smoke
Which meat is most closely linked with Texas?
Ribs with a dry spice rub

title: Life in the Gig Economy
p: Open a food delivery app in any large British or American city and, within minutes, a rider on a bicycle or scooter will be on the way.
在任何一座英美大城市打开外卖应用，几分钟之内，就会有一名骑自行车或电动车的骑手上路。
These riders are part of the so-called gig economy, in which people take on short, flexible jobs through digital platforms rather than working for a single employer.
这些骑手属于所谓的“零工经济”：人们通过数字平台承接短期、灵活的工作，而不是受雇于单一雇主。
For students and people with other commitments, the appeal is obvious: they can log on whenever it suits them.
对学生和有其他事务要兼顾的人来说，它的吸引力显而易见：想什么时候上线都可以。
Yet critics argue that this flexibility comes at a cost.
然而批评者认为，这种灵活是有代价的。
Because platforms often classify workers as independent contractors, many have not traditionally received sick pay, holiday pay or a guaranteed minimum income.
由于平台通常把劳动者归类为独立承包人，许多人过去一直得不到病假工资、带薪假期或有保障的最低收入。
Their earnings may also depend on algorithms they do not fully understand.
他们的收入还可能取决于他们并不完全了解的算法。
Courts and lawmakers in several countries have been reconsidering how such workers should be treated.
多个国家的法院和立法者一直在重新考虑应如何对待这类劳动者。
In a landmark 2021 ruling, the UK Supreme Court decided that Uber drivers were "workers" entitled to basic rights such as the minimum wage.
在 2021 年一项具有里程碑意义的判决中，英国最高法院裁定优步司机属于“劳动者”，有权享有最低工资等基本权利。
The central question remains unresolved: how to protect workers without losing the flexibility that attracted them in the first place.
核心问题仍未解决：如何既保护劳动者，又不失去当初吸引他们的那份灵活性。
q: Why is gig work attractive to students?
They can choose when to work
What did the UK Supreme Court decide in 2021?
Uber drivers were workers entitled to basic rights
What is the main question that remains unresolved?
How to protect workers while keeping flexibility
Which app is the most popular

title: The NHS: A National Treasure Under Pressure
zh: 压力下的“国宝”：英国国民医疗服务体系
p: When the National Health Service was launched on July 5, 1948, it was based on a simple yet radical idea: good healthcare should be available to everyone, regardless of wealth.
1948 年 7 月 5 日国民医疗服务体系（NHS）成立时，它基于一个简单却激进的理念：无论贫富，人人都应获得良好的医疗。
Funded mainly through general taxation, it is free at the point of use for UK residents, meaning patients do not pay to see a family doctor (GP) or to be treated in a hospital.
它主要靠一般税收提供资金，英国居民就医时免费，也就是说，看家庭医生（GP）或住院治疗都不用付钱。
The NHS is one of the largest employers in the world, and many Britons regard it with deep affection.
NHS 是世界上最大的雇主之一，许多英国人对它怀有深厚的感情。
During the opening ceremony of the 2012 London Olympics, hundreds of real nurses and hospital staff danced across the stadium in tribute.
在 2012 年伦敦奥运会开幕式上，数百名真正的护士和医院员工在体育场中翩翩起舞，向它致敬。
Still, the system faces persistent pressure.
尽管如此，这一体系始终承受着压力。
An aging population, rising costs and long waiting lists are constant subjects of political debate.
人口老龄化、成本上升和漫长的候诊名单，一直是政治辩论的话题。
Some services, such as prescriptions in England and most dental care, do involve charges, a detail that often surprises newcomers.
有些服务确实要收费，比如英格兰的处方药和大多数牙科治疗，这一点常常让新来的人感到意外。
q: How is the NHS mainly funded?
What happened at the 2012 London Olympics opening ceremony?
Nurses and hospital staff performed as a tribute
Which statement is true according to the article?
Some services, like prescriptions in England, involve charges
Everything in the NHS is completely free
Only wealthy people can use the NHS

title: Burns Night: Haggis, Poetry and Pipes
zh: 彭斯之夜：哈吉斯、诗歌与风笛
p: Every year on January 25, Scots around the world gather to celebrate the birthday of Robert Burns, Scotland's national poet, who was born in 1759.
每年 1 月 25 日，世界各地的苏格兰人都会聚在一起，庆祝苏格兰民族诗人罗伯特·彭斯的生日——他生于 1759 年。
A Burns Supper follows a well-loved order of events, and at its heart is the haggis — a savory pudding of sheep's offal, oats, onion and spices, traditionally cooked in a sheep's stomach.
彭斯晚宴遵循一套广受喜爱的流程，核心是哈吉斯——一种用羊杂、燕麦、洋葱和香料做成的咸味布丁，传统上装在羊胃里烹制。
The haggis is often carried in to the sound of bagpipes.
哈吉斯常常在风笛声中被端进来。
Then someone recites Burns's poem "Address to a Haggis," and at the line about cutting it open, the speaker plunges a knife dramatically into it.
接着有人朗诵彭斯的诗《致哈吉斯》，念到切开它的那一句时，朗诵者会夸张地一刀扎下去。
It is served with "neeps and tatties" — mashed swede (rutabaga) and potatoes — and often a glass of Scotch whisky.
它配着“neeps and tatties”——芜菁甘蓝泥和土豆泥——一起上桌，往往还有一杯苏格兰威士忌。
The evening includes speeches, toasts and more poetry, and it traditionally ends with everyone joining hands to sing "Auld Lang Syne," a song Burns wrote down and helped make famous.
当晚还有致辞、祝酒和更多的诗，传统上以大家手拉手合唱《友谊地久天长》结束——这首歌由彭斯记录整理并使之广为流传。
Curiously, the song is now heard far more often on New Year's Eve, in countries where few people know much about the poet himself.
有趣的是，如今这首歌更常在新年前夜响起，而在那些国家，很少有人了解这位诗人本身。
q: Why is Burns Night held on January 25?
It is the day haggis was invented
It is the first day of spring
What happens when the poem reaches the line about cutting the haggis?
The speaker cuts into it dramatically
What does the writer find curious about "Auld Lang Syne"?
It is now sung mostly on New Year's Eve around the world
It is only sung in Scotland
It has no connection to Burns

title: Voices in the Tower
p: From a dimly lit room near a major airport, an air traffic controller may be responsible for many aircraft at once, each carrying hundreds of lives.
在大型机场附近一间灯光昏暗的房间里，一名空中交通管制员可能同时负责许多架飞机，每架都载着数百条生命。
The job is to keep planes safely separated while guiding them through takeoff, landing and the crowded skies in between.
这份工作就是在引导飞机起飞、降落以及穿越其间拥挤空域的同时，让它们保持安全间隔。
Because pilots and controllers come from every corner of the globe, international rules require English to be available for radio communication on international flights.
由于飞行员和管制员来自世界各地，国际规则要求国际航班的无线电通话必须能使用英语。
To avoid confusion over a crackling radio, they use a standard phonetic alphabet — Alpha, Bravo, Charlie — and fixed phrases such as "Roger" and "Say again."
为了避免在噼啪作响的无线电中产生误解，他们使用标准的字母解读法——Alpha、Bravo、Charlie——以及“Roger（收到）”“Say again（请重复）”等固定用语。
Even numbers are pronounced in special ways: "nine" becomes "niner" so that it is not mistaken for another word on a poor connection.
连数字的读法都很特别：“nine”要读作“niner”，以免在信号差时被误听成别的词。
The work demands intense concentration, so controllers take regular breaks and their working hours are strictly limited.
这份工作需要高度集中注意力，所以管制员会定时休息，工作时长也受到严格限制。
Many describe it as calm problem-solving rather than constant panic — though a single mistake can carry enormous consequences.
许多人说，这份工作是冷静地解决问题，而不是一直手忙脚乱——尽管一个失误就可能造成严重后果。
q: What is the main job of an air traffic controller?
Why do controllers use a phonetic alphabet?
To avoid confusion over the radio
Why are controllers' working hours strictly limited?
They are paid by the hour

title: Think Before You Share
p: A dramatic photo of a shark swimming down a flooded highway seems to appear online after almost every major hurricane — and it is almost always fake.
一张鲨鱼在被淹的公路上游动的惊人照片，似乎在几乎每次大飓风之后都会出现在网上——而它几乎总是假的。
Such posts show how easily false information spreads on social media, often much faster than the corrections that follow.
这类帖子说明了虚假信息在社交媒体上传播得有多容易，往往比随后的更正快得多。
Part of the problem lies in how platforms work.
问题部分在于平台的运作方式。
Algorithms tend to promote content that triggers strong emotions such as anger, fear or amazement, because it keeps users scrolling.
算法倾向于推送能激起愤怒、恐惧或惊奇等强烈情绪的内容，因为这能让用户不停地往下刷。
A sensational claim that confirms what people already believe is particularly likely to be shared without being checked.
一个耸人听闻、又恰好印证人们原有看法的说法，尤其容易未经核实就被转发。
Fact-checkers and teachers now encourage a habit known as "lateral reading": instead of studying a single page closely, open new tabs to see what other reliable sources say about it.
事实核查人员和教师现在提倡一种叫“横向阅读”的习惯：不要只盯着一个页面细看，而是打开新标签页，看看其他可靠来源怎么说。
Simply pausing to ask who made a post, and why, can do a surprising amount to slow the spread of misinformation.
只要停下来问问这条帖子是谁发的、为什么发，就能在减缓错误信息传播方面起到惊人的作用。
q: Why do algorithms often promote misleading posts?
Checking what other sources say about a claim
Reading posts from left to right
What is the shark photo used to show?

title: Best Before or Use By?
zh: “最佳食用期”还是“食用截止期”？
p: British households throw away a huge amount of food every year, and a surprising share of it is perfectly safe to eat.
英国家庭每年扔掉大量食物，其中相当一部分其实完全可以安全食用。
One reason is confusion over the dates printed on packaging.
原因之一是人们搞不清包装上印的日期。
A "use by" date is about safety.
“use by（食用截止日期）”关乎安全。
It appears on foods that spoil quickly, such as fresh meat, fish and ready meals, and after that date they should not be eaten, even if they look and smell fine.
它出现在鲜肉、鱼和即食餐等容易变质的食品上；过了这个日期就不应再吃，即使看起来、闻起来都没问题。
A "best before" date, by contrast, is about quality.
相比之下，“best before（最佳食用日期）”关乎品质。
After it, bread may be slightly stale and potato chips less crunchy, but they are generally still safe to eat.
过了这个日期，面包可能有点不新鲜，薯片也不那么脆了，但一般仍可安全食用。
To reduce waste, several major UK supermarkets have removed "best before" dates from many fruits and vegetables, encouraging shoppers to judge freshness for themselves.
为了减少浪费，英国几家大型超市已去掉许多水果和蔬菜上的“最佳食用日期”，鼓励顾客自己判断新鲜程度。
In the United States, the system is even less consistent, because, apart from infant formula, date labels are largely not required by federal law.
在美国，这套体系更加不统一，因为除婴儿配方奶粉外，联邦法律基本不强制要求标注日期。
Campaigners argue that clearer labels could save families money and reduce the environmental cost of producing food that nobody eats.
倡导者认为，更清楚的标签既能帮家庭省钱，也能减少生产无人食用的食物所带来的环境代价。
q: What is a "use by" date about?
What have some UK supermarkets done?
Removed best-before dates from many fruits and vegetables
Added use-by dates to potato chips
What is true about date labels in the US?
Except on infant formula, they are largely not required by federal law
They are exactly the same as in the UK
They are printed only on fruit

title: The Gap Year Debate
p: In Britain, it is common for some young people to take a "gap year" between finishing school and starting university.
在英国，有些年轻人会在中学毕业和上大学之间休一个“间隔年”，这很常见。
A gap year might involve volunteering abroad, working to save money, or traveling on a tight budget.
间隔年里，他们可能去海外做志愿者、打工攒钱，或者穷游。
Supporters argue that a year away from the classroom helps students mature, discover what they genuinely want to study, and arrive at university more motivated.
支持者认为，离开课堂一年有助于学生变得成熟，弄清自己真正想学什么，进入大学时也更有动力。
Many universities accept deferred applications, allowing students to secure a place before taking time off.
许多大学接受延期入学申请，学生可以先确定录取资格再去休整。
Prince William and Prince Harry both took gap years, which helped make the idea more widely familiar.
威廉王子和哈里王子都休过间隔年，这让这一做法更加广为人知。

Critics, however, point out that expensive overseas trips are mainly available to students from wealthier families, and some volunteering projects have been accused of benefiting the volunteers more than local communities.
然而批评者指出，昂贵的海外旅行主要是富裕家庭的学生才负担得起，而且一些志愿项目被指责让志愿者受益多于当地社区。
As a result, many young people now spend their gap year closer to home, combining paid work with a short course or local volunteering.
因此，现在许多年轻人选择在离家更近的地方度过间隔年，一边打工赚钱，一边上短期课程或在本地做志愿者。
q: When do British students usually take a gap year?
In their first year of school
What does a deferred application allow students to do?
Secure a university place and start a year later
Apply to two universities at once
Which criticism of gap years is mentioned?
Expensive trips mainly suit wealthier students
Gap years are illegal in Britain

title: Juneteenth: Freedom Delayed
p: On June 19, 1865, Union soldiers arrived in Galveston, Texas, and announced that enslaved people in the state were free.
1865 年 6 月 19 日，北方联邦军队抵达得克萨斯州的加尔维斯顿，宣布该州被奴役的人获得自由。
Remarkably, this came more than two years after President Abraham Lincoln's Emancipation Proclamation took effect on January 1, 1863.
值得注意的是，这距离林肯总统的《解放黑人奴隶宣言》于 1863 年 1 月 1 日生效，已经过去了两年多。
News had traveled slowly, and freedom in practice depended on the arrival of Union troops.
消息传得很慢，而自由能否真正落实，取决于联邦军队何时到达。
The following year, freed people in Texas began celebrating the anniversary, calling it "Juneteenth," a blend of "June" and "nineteenth."
第二年，得克萨斯州获得自由的人们开始庆祝这个纪念日，称之为“Juneteenth”，由“June（六月）”和“nineteenth（十九日）”合成。
Over the decades, celebrations spread across the country, featuring picnics, parades, music, readings of the proclamation, and red foods and drinks such as strawberry soda and red velvet cake.
几十年间，庆祝活动遍及全国，有野餐、游行、音乐、宣读宣言，还有草莓汽水、红丝绒蛋糕等红色的食物和饮料。
In 2021, Juneteenth became a federal holiday, the first new one since Martin Luther King Jr. Day was established in 1983.
2021 年，六月节成为联邦假日，这是自 1983 年设立马丁·路德·金纪念日以来的第一个新联邦假日。
For many Americans, it is both a joyful celebration of freedom and a moment to reflect on how long that freedom took to arrive.
对许多美国人来说，这一天既是欢庆自由的日子，也是反思这份自由来得多么迟缓的时刻。
q: What happened in Galveston on June 19, 1865?
Enslaved people in Texas were told they were free
Where does the name "Juneteenth" come from?
The name of a Union general
When did Juneteenth become a federal holiday?

title: A Peanut Butter and Jelly Sandwich
p: Many American children eat a PB&J sandwich for lunch.
很多美国孩子午饭吃花生酱果酱三明治。
PB&J means peanut butter and jelly.
PB&J 的意思是花生酱和果酱。
You put peanut butter on one piece of bread and jelly on the other.
你在一片面包上抹花生酱，在另一片上抹果酱。
Then you press the two pieces together.
然后把两片面包合在一起。
The sandwich is cheap, sweet and very easy to make.
这种三明治便宜、甜，而且做起来非常简单。
Parents often put it in a paper bag with an apple and a juice box.
父母常常把它和一个苹果、一盒果汁一起装进纸袋里。
But some children cannot eat peanuts, so some schools do not allow them.
但是有些孩子不能吃花生，所以有些学校不允许带花生。
q: What do parents often put in the bag with the sandwich?
An apple and a juice box
Why do some schools not allow peanuts?

title: The Red Double-Decker Bus
p: London is famous for its red buses.
伦敦以红色巴士闻名。
Many of them are double-deckers, so they have two floors.
其中很多是双层巴士，也就是有两层。
You get on at the front and show your card to the driver's reader.
你从前门上车，在司机旁边的读卡器上刷卡。
You cannot pay with cash on London buses.
在伦敦坐巴士不能用现金付钱。
Many visitors like to sit at the front of the top floor.
很多游客喜欢坐在上层的最前面。
From there, you can see shops, parks and people in the street below.
从那里，你可以看到下面街上的商店、公园和行人。
It is like a cheap tour of the city.
这就像一次便宜的城市观光。
When you want to get off, you press the red button.
想下车时，就按红色的按钮。
q: How can you NOT pay on a London bus?
What do you do when you want to get off?

title: Vegemite on Toast
p: Vegemite is a dark brown spread from Australia.
Vegemite（维吉米特酱）是一种来自澳大利亚的深棕色涂抹酱。
It is made from yeast, and it tastes very salty.
它是用酵母做的，味道很咸。
Australians have eaten it since the 1920s.
澳大利亚人从二十世纪二十年代就开始吃它了。
Most people eat it on hot toast with butter.
大多数人把它抹在涂了黄油的热吐司上吃。
The secret is to use only a thin layer.
秘诀是只抹薄薄的一层。
Some visitors put on too much, and they do not like the strong taste.
有些游客抹得太多，就不喜欢那股浓烈的味道。
But many Australian children grow up with it and love it.
但是很多澳大利亚孩子从小吃它长大，非常喜欢。
q: What is the secret to eating Vegemite?
Eat it cold from the jar

title: Snow Day!
p: In Canada and the northern United States, winters can be very snowy.
在加拿大和美国北部，冬天可能雪很多。
Sometimes there is so much snow that the roads are not safe.
有时候雪太大，路面不安全。
Then the schools close for the day, and children call it a snow day.
这时学校会停课一天，孩子们把它叫做“雪天假”。
Early in the morning, families listen to the radio or check the school website.
一大早，家人们会听广播或查看学校网站。
When children hear the good news, they cheer.
孩子们听到这个好消息时会欢呼。
They put on warm boots and go outside to build snowmen.
他们穿上暖和的靴子，出去堆雪人。
Some ride sleds down a hill and come home with red cheeks.
有的人坐雪橇滑下山坡，回家时脸蛋冻得红红的。
q: Why do schools close on a snow day?
How do families find out about a snow day?
From the radio or the school website
From a letter the week before
From the newspaper the next day

title: Pull the Christmas Cracker
p: In Britain, there is a Christmas cracker next to every plate at Christmas dinner.
在英国，圣诞晚餐时每个盘子旁边都放着一个圣诞拉炮。
It looks like a big candy in shiny paper.
它看起来像一颗包着亮闪闪纸的大糖果。
Two people hold one end each and pull hard.
两个人各拿一端，用力拉。
Bang! The cracker breaks with a small pop.
砰！拉炮“啪”的一声断开了。
Inside, there is a paper crown, a small toy and a joke.
里面有一顶纸王冠、一个小玩具和一个笑话。
Everyone wears the paper crown during the meal, even grandpa.
吃饭时每个人都戴着纸王冠，连爷爷也戴。
The jokes are usually very bad, but that is part of the fun.
笑话通常很冷，但这正是乐趣的一部分。
q: How many people pull one cracker?
What is NOT inside a cracker?
What does the text say about the jokes?

title: Saturday at the Farmers' Market
p: Many towns in America and Canada have a farmers' market on Saturday morning.
美国和加拿大的很多小镇在周六上午有农贸集市。
Farmers bring fruit, vegetables, eggs and honey from their farms.
农民们从自己的农场带来水果、蔬菜、鸡蛋和蜂蜜。
They sell them at small tables under white tents.
他们在白色帐篷下的小桌子上卖东西。
The food is fresh because it was picked only a day or two ago.
食物很新鲜，因为它们一两天前才采摘下来。
You can talk to the farmer and ask how the food was grown.
你可以和农民聊天，问问这些食物是怎么种出来的。
Some stalls also sell bread, flowers and homemade jam.
有些摊位还卖面包、鲜花和自制果酱。
Often there is music, and families stay for a coffee or a snack.
那里常常有音乐，一家人会留下来喝杯咖啡或吃点小吃。
q: When do many towns have a farmers' market?
It was picked a day or two ago
It is kept in a freezer
It is sold in plastic boxes
What can you do at the market besides shopping?
Talk to farmers and listen to music

title: Sweet Maple Syrup
p: Maple syrup comes from maple trees.
枫糖浆来自枫树。
In early spring, farmers make a small hole in each tree and collect the sap.
早春时节，农民在每棵树上钻一个小孔，收集树液。
They boil the sap for many hours until it becomes thick and sweet.
他们把树液熬上好几个小时，直到它变得又稠又甜。
It takes about forty liters of sap to make one liter of syrup!
大约四十升树液才能熬出一升糖浆！
Canada makes most of the world's maple syrup, and most of it comes from Quebec.
世界上大部分枫糖浆产自加拿大，其中大部分来自魁北克。
People pour it on pancakes and waffles.
人们把它浇在薄煎饼和华夫饼上。
In spring, families visit a sugar shack and eat maple taffy made on fresh snow.
春天，一家人会去“糖屋”，吃在新雪上做成的枫糖太妃。
q: When do farmers collect the sap?
How much sap makes one liter of syrup?
Where does most of the world's maple syrup come from?

title: The Sausage Sizzle
p: A sausage sizzle is a simple barbecue in Australia.
“香肠烧烤”是澳大利亚一种简单的烧烤活动。
Volunteers cook sausages and onions on a hot plate outside a shop or a school.
志愿者们在商店或学校外面的铁板上烤香肠和洋葱。
They put each sausage on a slice of white bread with tomato sauce.
他们把每根香肠放在一片白面包上，再加上番茄酱。
The money usually helps a sports club, a school or a charity.
赚到的钱通常用来帮助体育俱乐部、学校或慈善机构。
On election day, many voting places have a sausage sizzle too.
在选举日，很多投票站也会办香肠烧烤。
Australians call it a "democracy sausage."
澳大利亚人把它叫做“民主香肠”。
People vote, buy a sausage and eat it while they walk home.
人们投完票，买根香肠，边走回家边吃。
q: Who usually cooks at a sausage sizzle?
Where does the money usually go?
To a club, a school or a charity
A sausage sold at a voting place
A sausage made by the government

title: Show and Tell
p: In many American and British primary schools, children have show and tell.
在很多美国和英国的小学里，孩子们有“展示与讲述”活动。
Each child brings something special from home.
每个孩子从家里带一样特别的东西。
It may be a toy, a shell from the beach or a photo of a new baby.
可能是一个玩具、一个从海滩捡来的贝壳，或者一张新生宝宝的照片。
The child stands in front of the class and talks about it.
孩子站在全班同学面前介绍它。
The other children sit on the carpet and listen.
其他孩子坐在地毯上听。
Then they ask questions, like "Where did you get it?"
然后他们会提问，比如“你是从哪里得到它的？”
Show and tell helps young children learn to speak in front of other people.
展示与讲述帮助小孩子学会在别人面前说话。
q: What does each child bring to show and tell?
Where do the other children sit?
What does show and tell help children learn?
To speak in front of other people

title: The Fourth of July
p: July 4 is Independence Day in the United States.
七月四日是美国的独立日。
On this day in 1776, the Declaration of Independence was adopted.
1776 年的这一天，《独立宣言》获得通过。
Today it is a big summer holiday, and most people do not work.
如今，这是一个盛大的夏日节日，大多数人不用上班。
Towns have parades with bands, old cars and fire trucks.
各个小镇会举行游行，有乐队、老爷车和消防车。
Families have picnics and cook hot dogs and hamburgers on the grill.
一家人去野餐，在烤架上烤热狗和汉堡。
Many houses hang a red, white and blue flag.
很多人家门前挂着红、白、蓝三色的国旗。
At night, everyone looks up at the fireworks.
到了晚上，大家都抬头看烟花。
q: The Declaration of Independence was adopted
The first hot dog was made
What do families often cook on the Fourth of July?
What does everyone look at at night?

title: Mind the Gap: Riding the Tube
zh: 小心空隙：乘坐伦敦地铁
p: London's underground railway, known as the Tube, opened in 1863, making it the oldest in the world.
伦敦的地下铁路被称为“the Tube”，于 1863 年开通，是世界上最古老的地铁。
Today it carries millions of passengers every day through dozens of tunnels and stations.
如今，它每天通过几十条隧道和众多车站运送数百万乘客。
Its red circle and blue bar logo is one of the most famous signs in the city.
它红圈加蓝条的标志是这座城市最著名的标识之一。
On many platforms, you will hear a recorded voice saying, "Mind the gap."
在很多站台上，你会听到录音说：“Mind the gap（小心空隙）。”
It warns passengers about the space between the train and the curved platform edge.
它提醒乘客注意列车与弯曲站台边缘之间的空隙。
Regular riders also follow unwritten rules, such as standing on the right on escalators so others can walk past on the left.
常坐地铁的人还遵守一些不成文的规矩，比如在自动扶梯上靠右站，让别人从左边走过。
Breaking this rule during the morning rush is a sure way to annoy a commuter.
在早高峰时违反这条规矩，肯定会惹恼上班族。
q: What is special about the Tube?
It is the oldest underground railway in the world
It is the longest railway in the world
Why does a voice say "Mind the gap"?
To warn people about the space between the train and the platform
To tell people the train is late
To ask people to buy a ticket
To tell people to stand on the left
On escalators, where should you stand?

title: Life in a Terraced House
p: Walk through almost any British town and you will see long rows of terraced houses.
走过几乎任何一座英国城镇，你都会看到一排排长长的联排房屋。
Each house shares its side walls with its neighbors, so the whole street looks like one long building.
每栋房子都与邻居共用侧墙，所以整条街看起来像一栋长长的建筑。
Most were built in the Victorian era, when factories needed cheap homes for millions of workers.
其中大多数建于维多利亚时代，当时工厂需要为数百万工人提供廉价住房。
A typical small terrace is called a "two-up, two-down," with two rooms upstairs and two downstairs.
一种典型的小型联排房被称为“上二下二”，楼上两个房间，楼下两个房间。
Early ones had no bathroom, and families used a toilet in the back yard.
早期的房子没有浴室，一家人只能用后院的厕所。
Today these houses have been modernized and are popular with young couples.
如今这些房子已经过现代化改造，很受年轻夫妇欢迎。
The only downside is that you can sometimes hear your neighbor's television through the wall.
唯一的缺点是，有时你能隔着墙听到邻居家的电视声。
q: Why were so many terraced houses built?
People wanted to live in the countryside
A house with two rooms upstairs and two downstairs
A house with two front doors
A street with two rows of houses
A house shared by two families
What is one downside of living in a terrace today?
You may hear your neighbor through the wall
It is very far from town
It is too big to heat

title: Friday Night Lights
p: In many small American towns, the most exciting event of the week happens on Friday night in the fall.
在美国许多小镇，每周最激动人心的活动发生在秋天的周五晚上。
That is when the local high school football team plays under bright stadium lights.
那时，当地高中的橄榄球队会在明亮的体育场灯光下比赛。
Parents, grandparents and neighbors who have no children at the school all fill the stands.
家长、祖父母，甚至没有孩子在这所学校上学的邻居，都会坐满看台。
The game is about much more than football.
比赛的意义远不止橄榄球本身。
The marching band performs at halftime, cheerleaders lead the crowd, and students sell snacks to raise money for school clubs.
中场休息时乐队进行行进表演，啦啦队带动观众，学生们卖零食为学校社团筹款。
Once a year, the school holds a homecoming game, when former students return to cheer for their old team.
学校每年举办一次“返校节”比赛，校友们会回来为母校的球队加油。
For many towns, the team is a source of pride that brings the whole community together.
对很多小镇来说，球队是一种骄傲，把整个社区凝聚在一起。
q: When do high school football games usually take place?
On Friday nights in the fall
What happens at a homecoming game?
What is the main idea of the text?
High school football brings small towns together
Football is too dangerous for students
Marching bands are more popular than football

title: A Night to Remember: The Prom
p: For many American teenagers, the prom is the biggest social event of high school.
对很多美国青少年来说，毕业舞会是高中最盛大的社交活动。
The word comes from "promenade," an old term for a formal walk or dance.
这个词来自“promenade”，是一个指正式散步或舞会的古老词语。
It is usually held in spring for students in their last one or two years of school.
它通常在春天举行，对象是最后一两年的高中生。
Preparation can take weeks.
准备工作可能要花好几周。
Girls shop for dresses, boys rent tuxedos, and some students ask their dates in creative ways, a custom called a "promposal."
女孩们选购礼服，男孩们租燕尾服，有些学生还会用有创意的方式邀请舞伴，这种习俗叫做“舞会邀约”。
On the night, couples often exchange flowers: a corsage for the wrist and a boutonniere for the jacket.
当晚，舞伴们常常互赠鲜花：戴在手腕上的腕花和别在外套上的胸花。
Near the end, students vote for a prom king and queen, and parents wait nervously for their children to come home safely.
临近结束时，学生们投票选出舞会国王和王后，而家长们则紧张地等着孩子平安回家。
q: Where does the word "prom" come from?
Promenade, a formal walk or dance
Program, because it has a schedule
A creative way of asking someone to the prom
A vote for the prom queen

title: Super Bowl Sunday
p: The Super Bowl, the championship game of the National Football League, is played every year in early February.
超级碗是美国国家橄榄球联盟的总决赛，每年二月初举行。
It is not an official holiday, but for many Americans it feels like one.
它不是法定节日，但对很多美国人来说，感觉就像过节一样。
It is regularly one of the most-watched television broadcasts of the year in the country.
它常常是全美一年中收视率最高的电视节目之一。
Few people watch alone; instead, friends gather for Super Bowl parties.
很少有人独自观看，朋友们会聚在一起开超级碗派对。
Tables are covered with chicken wings, nachos, chips and dip, and pizza.
桌上摆满了鸡翅、玉米片、薯片配蘸酱和比萨。
Even people who do not care about football tune in for two other attractions: the halftime show, featuring major pop stars, and the commercials.
就连不关心橄榄球的人也会为另外两大看点收看：有大牌流行歌星登台的中场秀，以及广告。
Companies spend huge sums on these ads, and the funniest ones are discussed at work the next morning.
公司在这些广告上花费巨资，第二天早上大家会在单位里讨论最好笑的那几条。
q: The championship game of the NFL
Why do people who don't like football watch it?
For the halftime show and the commercials
Because they have to by law
Because there is nothing else on TV
What happens the morning after the game?
People talk about the funniest ads at work

title: Poutine: Canada's Messy Favorite
zh: 肉汁奶酪薯条：加拿大的“一团糟”美食
p: Poutine is a simple dish from Quebec: French fries topped with cheese curds and covered in hot brown gravy.
肉汁奶酪薯条是来自魁北克的一道简单的菜：炸薯条上铺着奶酪凝乳，再浇上热腾腾的棕色肉汁。
It first appeared in rural Quebec in the 1950s, although several small towns claim to have invented it.
它最早于二十世纪五十年代出现在魁北克的乡村，不过有好几个小镇都声称是自己发明的。
For years, some people looked down on it as cheap, greasy food.
很多年来，一些人瞧不起它，认为它是廉价又油腻的食物。
The secret is the cheese curds, which should be so fresh that they squeak between your teeth.
秘诀在于奶酪凝乳，它要新鲜到在牙齿间咬得吱吱作响。
The hot gravy softens them just a little without melting them completely.
热肉汁只会让它们稍微变软，而不会完全融化。
Today poutine is sold everywhere from roadside trucks to fancy restaurants, which add toppings like pulled pork or even lobster.
如今从路边餐车到高档餐厅到处都有卖，高档餐厅还会加上手撕猪肉甚至龙虾等配料。
Many Canadians consider it a national comfort food, especially after a long winter night.
很多加拿大人把它视为国民慰藉食物，尤其是在漫长的冬夜之后。
q: What are the three main parts of poutine?
How can you tell that the cheese curds are fresh?
How has the image of poutine changed?
It went from cheap food to something served even in fancy restaurants
It used to be expensive but is now cheap
It is now banned in Quebec
It is now only eaten at breakfast

title: What Is Boxing Day?
p: December 26 is Boxing Day, a public holiday in Britain, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and several other countries.
12 月 26 日是节礼日，在英国、加拿大、澳大利亚、新西兰和其他一些国家是公共假日。
Despite the name, it has nothing to do with the sport of boxing.
尽管名字如此，它和拳击运动毫无关系。
Historians are not completely sure where the name comes from, but a common explanation is that employers once gave servants and workers a "Christmas box" of money or gifts on this day.
历史学家并不完全确定这个名字的由来，但一种常见的说法是，过去雇主会在这一天给仆人和工人一个装有钱或礼物的“圣诞盒”。
Today the day has its own traditions.
如今，这一天有它自己的传统。
Many people eat leftovers from Christmas dinner and go for a long walk to recover from all the food.
很多人吃圣诞晚餐的剩菜，然后去走很长一段路来消化那么多食物。
Stores hold huge sales, and some shoppers line up before dawn to get the best deals.
商店举行大促销，有些购物者天亮前就开始排队抢最划算的商品。
Sports fans have plenty to watch too: in England there is a full program of football matches, and in Australia the famous Boxing Day Test cricket match begins in Melbourne.
体育迷也有很多比赛可看：英格兰有一整轮足球赛，澳大利亚墨尔本则会开打著名的节礼日板球对抗赛。
q: What does Boxing Day have to do with boxing?
It is the day of the biggest boxing match
It started as a boxing festival
According to a common explanation, what was a "Christmas box"?
Money or gifts given to servants and workers
A box used to store decorations
Which of these is NOT mentioned as a Boxing Day activity?

title: Anzac Biscuits
p: Anzac biscuits are sweet, chewy cookies loved in Australia and New Zealand.
澳新军团饼干是一种香甜有嚼劲的饼干，深受澳大利亚和新西兰人喜爱。
They are named after the ANZACs, the soldiers of the Australian and New Zealand Army Corps who fought in the First World War.
它们以“ANZAC”命名，即在第一次世界大战中作战的澳大利亚和新西兰军团士兵。
Their main ingredients are rolled oats, flour, sugar, coconut, butter and golden syrup.
它们的主要原料是燕麦片、面粉、糖、椰丝、黄油和金黄糖浆。
Interestingly, the recipe contains no eggs.
有趣的是，这个配方里没有鸡蛋。
One popular explanation is that eggs were scarce during the war, and biscuits without them stayed fresh longer.
一种流行的解释是，战争期间鸡蛋稀缺，而且不放鸡蛋的饼干能保存得更久。
Families bake them especially around Anzac Day on April 25, when both countries remember those who served in war.
人们尤其会在 4 月 25 日澳新军团日前后烤这种饼干，那天两国都会纪念参战的军人。
People still argue happily about whether a good Anzac biscuit should be crunchy or soft.
人们至今仍乐此不疲地争论：好的澳新军团饼干应该是脆的还是软的。
q: Who are Anzac biscuits named after?
Which ingredient is NOT in the recipe?
When do families especially bake them?

title: The Full Irish Breakfast
p: Ask for a "full Irish" in a café in Ireland, and you will receive a very large plate.
在爱尔兰的咖啡馆点一份“full Irish”，你会得到满满一大盘。
It usually includes fried eggs, rashers of bacon, sausages, grilled tomato and mushrooms.
通常包括煎蛋、几片培根、香肠、烤番茄和蘑菇。
What makes it different from an English breakfast is the black and white pudding.
它与英式早餐的不同之处在于黑布丁和白布丁。
Despite the name, these puddings are not desserts at all.
尽管叫“布丁”，它们根本不是甜点。
They are round slices of sausage made with oats and pork, and black pudding also contains blood.
它们是用燕麦和猪肉做成的圆片香肠，黑布丁里还含有血。
The meal is served with soda bread, a quick bread that uses baking soda instead of yeast, and a strong pot of tea.
这顿饭配有苏打面包（一种用小苏打代替酵母的快速面包）和一壶浓茶。
It was originally a farmer's meal to give energy for a hard day of work, but today most people save it for a lazy weekend morning.
它原本是农民的饭，为一天的辛苦劳作提供能量，但如今大多数人会留到悠闲的周末早上才吃。
q: What makes a full Irish different from an English breakfast?
What is used instead of yeast in soda bread?
When do most people eat a full Irish today?
Before a hard day on the farm

title: Backyard Cricket
p: Every summer in Australia, families play a relaxed version of cricket in backyards, parks and on beaches.
在澳大利亚，每到夏天，家家户户都会在后院、公园和海滩上玩一种轻松版的板球。
Instead of a hard leather ball, they use a tennis ball, and a plastic garbage bin often serves as the wicket.
他们不用坚硬的皮球，而是用网球，常常用一个塑料垃圾桶当三柱门。
Players of all ages join in, from small children to grandparents.
从小孩子到祖父母，各个年龄段的人都会参加。
Backyard cricket has its own funny rules that change from family to family.
后院板球有自己的趣味规则，每家都不一样。
A common one is "six and out": if you hit the ball over the fence, you score six runs but are out because someone has to go and find the ball.
常见的一条是“六分出局”：如果你把球打过围栏，你得六分，但同时出局，因为得有人去把球找回来。
Another rule allows players to be caught out with "one hand, one bounce," so even small children can take a catch.
另一条规则是“单手一次弹地”也算接杀出局，这样连小孩子也能接住球。
For many Australians, these games are where a lifelong love of the sport begins.
对很多澳大利亚人来说，正是这些游戏开启了他们对这项运动一生的热爱。
q: What is often used as the wicket in backyard cricket?
Why is a player out after hitting the ball over the fence?
Someone has to go and find the ball
What is the purpose of the "one hand, one bounce" rule?
To help small children catch players out
To let adults score more runs

title: The Truth About Black Friday
p: Black Friday is the day after Thanksgiving in the United States, and it marks the unofficial start of the Christmas shopping season.
黑色星期五是美国感恩节后的第一天，标志着圣诞购物季非正式的开始。
Stores open early and offer big discounts on TVs, toys and clothes.
商店很早开门，对电视、玩具和衣服大幅打折。
In the past, crowds camped outside stores overnight, and news reports showed shoppers fighting over the last bargains.
过去，人群会在商店外露营过夜，新闻报道里还出现过购物者争抢最后几件特价商品的画面。
Many people believe the name means that stores finally move "into the black," or start making a profit, on this day.
很多人以为这个名字的意思是商店在这一天终于“转为黑字”，也就是开始盈利。
In fact, the term was used earlier by police in Philadelphia, who dreaded the heavy traffic and huge crowds.
实际上，这个说法更早是由费城警察使用的，他们害怕这一天拥堵的交通和巨大的人潮。
Today the event has changed again, as more shoppers buy online and many deals last for a week or more.
如今，这个活动又发生了变化，越来越多的人网购，很多优惠会持续一周甚至更久。
It is now followed by Cyber Monday, a day focused on online shopping.
现在它之后还有“网络星期一”，专门针对网上购物。
q: The last Friday of the year
Who used the term "Black Friday" early on?
How has Black Friday changed recently?
More people shop online and deals last longer
Stores now close on that day
It has moved to the summer

title: The Hāngī: Cooking with the Earth
p: A hāngī is a traditional Māori way of cooking food in an earth oven in New Zealand.
地坑烤（hāngī）是新西兰毛利人在土灶里烹饪食物的传统方式。
First, a pit is dug in the ground, and volcanic stones are heated in a large fire until they glow.
首先在地上挖一个坑，把火山石放在大火里烧到通红。
The hot stones are placed in the pit, and baskets of meat and vegetables are set on top.
把烧热的石头放进坑里，再把装着肉和蔬菜的篮子放在上面。
Everything is covered with wet cloths and then with earth to trap the heat.
然后用湿布把所有东西盖住，再盖上泥土以锁住热量。
After about three hours, the food is dug up, tender and full of a smoky, earthy flavor.
大约三小时后把食物挖出来，口感软嫩，充满烟熏和泥土的风味。
Typical hāngī foods include pork, chicken, potatoes and kūmara, a type of sweet potato.
典型的地坑烤食物包括猪肉、鸡肉、土豆和库马拉（一种红薯）。
Because it takes so much work, a hāngī is usually prepared for large gatherings such as weddings, funerals and community celebrations.
因为工序繁多，地坑烤通常为婚礼、葬礼和社区庆典等大型聚会而准备。
q: What are heated in the fire for a hāngī?
Why is the food covered with earth?
Why is a hāngī usually made for large gatherings?
It takes a lot of work
It is illegal for small groups
It can only be made in winter

title: Built for the Car: The American Suburb
p: After the Second World War, millions of American families left crowded cities for newly built suburbs.
第二次世界大战后，数百万美国家庭离开拥挤的城市，搬进新建的郊区。
Developments such as Levittown in New York offered affordable houses with lawns and garages, built quickly on mass-production lines.
纽约的莱维敦等住宅区提供了带草坪和车库的平价住房，以流水线方式快速建成。
Meanwhile, the Interstate Highway System, approved in 1956, made it possible to live far from the office and drive to work.
与此同时，1956 年获批的州际公路系统让人们可以住得离办公室很远，开车上班。
The result is a landscape designed around the automobile.
其结果是一种以汽车为中心设计的景观。
Homes, schools and shops are often separated by zoning laws, so even buying a carton of milk can require a drive.
住宅、学校和商店常常被分区法规隔开，因此即使买一盒牛奶也可能需要开车。
Drive-through banks, pharmacies and restaurants allow people to run errands without leaving their seats, and most teenagers count down the days until they can get a driver's license.
得来速银行、药店和餐厅让人们不用离开座位就能办事，大多数青少年都在倒数拿到驾照的日子。
Critics argue that this pattern encourages traffic, pollution and isolation, especially for elderly people who can no longer drive.
批评者认为，这种模式助长了交通拥堵、污染和孤立，尤其是对已经不能开车的老年人而言。
In response, some towns are now building "walkable" neighborhoods with sidewalks, bike lanes and shops within reach of home.
作为回应，一些城镇正在建设“适宜步行”的社区，配有人行道、自行车道和步行可达的商店。
q: What made it possible for suburban families to drive long distances to work?
Why might buying milk require a drive in many suburbs?
Zoning laws separate homes from shops
Milk is only sold in cities
Stores do not allow people to walk in
Which group do critics say is especially affected by isolation?
Elderly people who can no longer drive
People who live in the city center

title: Treasure Hunting in Charity Shops
p: On almost every British high street, between the bakery and the bank, you will find at least one charity shop.
在几乎每条英国商业街上，在面包店和银行之间，你至少会找到一家慈善商店。
These stores sell second-hand clothes, books and household goods donated by the public, and the profits go to causes such as medical research or overseas aid.
这些商店出售公众捐赠的二手衣服、书籍和家居用品，利润用于医学研究或海外援助等公益事业。
Oxfam opened one of the country's first permanent charity shops in Oxford in the late 1940s, and the idea has since spread nationwide.
乐施会于二十世纪四十年代末在牛津开设了英国最早的常设慈善商店之一，此后这一模式遍及全国。
In North America the equivalent is the thrift store, and organizations such as Goodwill, founded in Boston in 1902, also use their stores to provide job training.
在北美，与之相当的是“节俭商店”，1902 年创立于波士顿的“善意”（Goodwill）等组织还利用门店提供职业培训。
For a long time, buying used clothing carried a certain stigma, suggesting that the shopper could not afford anything new.
很长一段时间里，买二手衣服带有某种污名，暗示购物者买不起新东西。
That attitude has shifted dramatically.
这种态度已经发生了巨大转变。
Concern about the environmental cost of fast fashion has made second-hand shopping fashionable, especially among young people.
对快时尚环境代价的担忧让二手购物变得时髦，尤其是在年轻人中。
Some even treat it as a hobby, searching the racks for vintage jackets or rare records, and sharing their best finds online.
有些人甚至把它当成爱好，在衣架间搜寻复古夹克或稀有唱片，并在网上分享自己的最佳收获。
q: Where do the profits of charity shops go?
To causes such as medical research or overseas aid
To the people who donate items
What does Goodwill provide besides second-hand goods?
Why has second-hand shopping become more popular among young people?
Concern about the environmental cost of fast fashion
New clothes are no longer sold
Charity shops pay people to shop

title: March Madness and the College Sports Machine
p: Every spring, tens of millions of Americans fill out brackets predicting the winners of the NCAA men's and women's college basketball tournaments.
每年春天，数千万美国人会填写对阵表，预测美国大学体育协会男子和女子大学篮球锦标赛的胜者。
Known as March Madness, the single-elimination format means that a small school can knock out a famous program in a single night.
这项赛事被称为“疯狂三月”，单场淘汰赛制意味着一所小学校可能在一夜之间淘汰一支名校强队。
Offices run friendly competitions, and productivity reportedly dips as workers check scores on their phones.
办公室里会组织友谊竞猜，据说工作效率会下降，因为员工们都在手机上查比分。
The tournament reflects how central sports are to American universities, something that surprises many visitors.
这项锦标赛反映出体育在美国大学中的核心地位，这让许多外国人感到惊讶。
Top football and basketball programs fill stadiums, earn enormous television revenue, and serve as a powerful way of attracting students and donors.
顶级橄榄球和篮球项目能坐满体育场，赚取巨额电视转播收入，也是吸引学生和捐款人的有力手段。
This success has long raised an awkward question: if the games generate so much money, should the athletes be paid?
这种成功长期以来引发了一个尴尬的问题：如果比赛能赚这么多钱，运动员是否应该获得报酬？
For decades, players received scholarships but were forbidden from profiting from their fame.
几十年来，球员们获得奖学金，却被禁止利用自己的名气获利。

Since 2021, however, athletes have been allowed to earn money from their name, image and likeness through sponsorships and advertising, and the debate over fairness continues to reshape college sports.
然而自 2021 年起，运动员被允许通过赞助和广告从自己的姓名、形象和肖像中获利，有关公平的争论仍在不断重塑大学体育。
q: What does the single-elimination format make possible?
A small school can beat a famous team and knock it out
Every team plays the same number of games
Teams can lose once and still continue
Why are sports programs important to American universities, according to the text?
They bring in money and attract students and donors
Athletes could earn money from their name, image and likeness
The tournament moved to the fall
Women's teams joined the NCAA for the first time
