title: Blazers and Ties: The British School Uniform
zh: 西装外套与领带：英国校服
p: Visitors to Britain are often struck by the sight of children in blazers, ties and pleated skirts walking to school.
来英国的游客常常对孩子们穿着西装外套、打着领带、穿着百褶裙上学的景象印象深刻。
Unlike in the United States, where uniforms are mostly found in private schools, the great majority of British state schools require them.
在美国，校服主要出现在私立学校，而英国绝大多数公立学校都要求穿校服。
The tradition is old: pupils at Christ's Hospital school still wear the long blue coats and yellow socks first introduced in the sixteenth century.
这一传统由来已久：基督公学的学生至今仍穿着十六世纪开始采用的蓝色长外套和黄色袜子。
Supporters argue that uniforms create a sense of belonging and reduce pressure on children to follow expensive fashion trends.
支持者认为，校服能营造归属感，并减轻孩子们追逐昂贵时尚潮流的压力。
Wearing the same clothes, they say, hides differences in family income and lets pupils concentrate on learning.
他们说，穿同样的衣服能掩盖家庭收入的差异，让学生专心学习。
Critics, however, point out that the cost can be a burden, especially when schools insist on branded items available from only one supplier.
然而批评者指出，校服费用可能成为负担，尤其是当学校坚持要求只能从唯一供应商购买带校徽的服装时。
Partly in response, a law passed in 2021 requires schools in England to keep uniform costs reasonable.
部分出于回应，2021 年通过的一项法律要求英格兰的学校将校服费用控制在合理范围内。
Debates also continue over gender rules, such as whether girls should be allowed to wear trousers.
关于性别方面的规定也一直存在争议，比如是否应允许女生穿长裤。
q: How is the British situation different from the American one?
Most British state schools require uniforms
British private schools never have uniforms
American state schools all require uniforms
What do supporters say uniforms can hide?
What does the 2021 law require schools in England to do?
Let pupils design their own uniforms

title: Christmas Down Under
p: For Australians and New Zealanders, Christmas falls in the middle of summer, which makes many northern traditions seem slightly absurd.
对澳大利亚人和新西兰人来说，圣诞节正值盛夏，这让许多北半球的传统显得有些荒诞。
Shops still decorate their windows with fake snow and pictures of reindeer, even as temperatures climb well above thirty degrees Celsius.
即使气温远超三十摄氏度，商店依然用人造雪和驯鹿图片装饰橱窗。
Christmas cards, too, often show snowy scenes that few locals have ever experienced on December 25.
圣诞贺卡上也常常是雪景，而当地人几乎没有人在 12 月 25 日见过这样的景象。
Over time, however, families have adapted the holiday to the climate.
然而，随着时间的推移，人们已让这个节日适应了当地的气候。
Instead of a heavy roast, many prefer cold meats, salads and fresh seafood, especially prawns, eaten outdoors.
许多人不吃厚重的烤肉，而更喜欢在户外吃冷切肉、沙拉和新鲜海鲜，尤其是大虾。
Dessert is frequently pavlova, a meringue cake topped with cream and summer fruit, whose origin both countries proudly claim.
甜点通常是帕芙洛娃，一种上面铺着奶油和夏季水果的蛋白霜蛋糕，两国都自豪地声称是它的发源地。
Some families spend the afternoon at the beach, and in Melbourne, Carols by Candlelight, an outdoor concert held on Christmas Eve, has been a tradition for decades.
有些家庭会在海滩上度过下午，而在墨尔本，平安夜举行的户外音乐会“烛光颂歌”已延续了数十年。
These customs show how a festival imported from the northern hemisphere has gradually developed a distinctly southern character.
这些习俗表明，一个从北半球传入的节日是如何逐渐形成鲜明的南半球特色的。
q: Why do some northern Christmas traditions seem absurd in Australia?
There are no shops in December
A meringue cake with cream and fruit
What is the main idea of the text?
Christmas in the south has developed its own character
Seafood is the most important part of Christmas

title: The Great Chowder Divide
p: Few dishes divide Americans as sharply as clam chowder.
很少有哪道菜像蛤蜊浓汤这样让美国人意见分歧如此尖锐。
The best-known version, New England clam chowder, is a thick, creamy white soup of clams, potatoes, onions and salt pork.
最著名的版本新英格兰蛤蜊浓汤是一种浓稠的奶白色汤，里面有蛤蜊、土豆、洋葱和咸猪肉。
Manhattan clam chowder, by contrast, replaces the cream with tomatoes, producing a thin red broth that looks more like vegetable soup.
相比之下，曼哈顿蛤蜊浓汤用番茄代替奶油，做出一种看起来更像蔬菜汤的清淡红色汤底。
Many New Englanders regard the tomato version as an outright insult to tradition.
许多新英格兰人认为番茄版本是对传统的公然侮辱。
The rivalry even reached politics: in 1939, a lawmaker in Maine reportedly proposed a bill to make it illegal to add tomatoes to chowder.
这种对立甚至波及政坛：据报道，1939 年缅因州一名议员提出了一项法案，要将在浓汤里加番茄定为违法。
The bill never became law, but the story is still told with relish.
这项法案从未成为法律，但这个故事至今仍被津津乐道。
Meanwhile, Rhode Island quietly serves its own clear-broth chowder, and San Francisco has made the dish famous by pouring it into a hollowed-out loaf of sourdough bread.
与此同时，罗得岛州默默地供应着自己的清汤版浓汤，而旧金山则把浓汤倒进掏空的酸面包里，让这道菜出了名。
These regional variations show how a single dish can become a symbol of local identity.
这些地区差异表明，一道菜可以成为地方身份认同的象征。
q: What is the main difference between New England and Manhattan clam chowder?
Manhattan chowder uses tomatoes instead of cream
New England chowder is served cold
New England chowder uses rice instead of potatoes
What happened to the 1939 bill in Maine?
It became law and is still enforced
It made chowder the state dish
How is chowder famously served in San Francisco?
In a hollowed-out loaf of sourdough bread

title: Growing Your Own: Britain's Allotments
p: On the edges of British towns and cities, you can often spot patchworks of small vegetable plots, each with its own shed and compost heap.
在英国城镇的边缘，你常常能看到一片片拼布般的小菜地，每块地都有自己的小棚屋和堆肥堆。
These are allotments: pieces of land rented, usually from the local council, to people who want to grow their own food.
这些就是份地：通常从地方议会租来的小块土地，租给想自己种菜的人。
Their roots lie partly in the nineteenth century, when plots were provided so that poor families could feed themselves.
它们的起源部分可以追溯到十九世纪，当时提供这些地块是为了让贫困家庭能自给自足。
Allotments reached their peak during the Second World War, when the government's "Dig for Victory" campaign urged citizens to turn every available patch of ground into a vegetable garden.
份地在第二次世界大战期间达到鼎盛，当时政府的“为胜利而挖”运动号召公民把每一块可用的空地都变成菜园。
After the war, interest declined, and many sites were sold for housing.
战后人们的兴趣下降，许多地块被卖掉用于建房。
In recent decades, however, allotments have enjoyed a remarkable revival, driven by interest in healthy eating, sustainability and simply escaping screens.
然而近几十年来，份地出现了显著的复兴，推动因素包括对健康饮食、可持续发展的兴趣，以及单纯想远离屏幕。
In many areas, waiting lists now stretch for years.
在许多地区，如今的排队名单要等好几年。
For plot holders, the reward is not only fresh produce but also a sense of community, as neighbors swap seeds, advice and the inevitable surplus of zucchini.
对租地者来说，回报不仅是新鲜的农产品，还有一种社区感，邻居们会交换种子、经验，以及不可避免地吃不完的西葫芦。
q: What was the aim of the "Dig for Victory" campaign?
To make citizens grow vegetables on available land
What shows that allotments are popular again today?
Waiting lists can stretch for years

title: Tex-Mex: A Cuisine of the Border
zh: 得州墨西哥菜：边境料理
p: Tex-Mex is the cooking of Texas's Mexican American community, known as Tejanos, and it has become one of the most popular cuisines in the United States.
得州墨西哥菜是得州墨西哥裔美国人社群（称为 Tejanos）的烹饪方式，已成为美国最受欢迎的菜系之一。
Although it grew out of Mexican traditions, it has its own distinct identity.
虽然它源自墨西哥传统，但有其独特的身份。
Compared with the food of central Mexico, it relies more heavily on beef, yellow cheese, cumin and wheat-flour tortillas.
与墨西哥中部的饮食相比，它更多地依赖牛肉、黄奶酪、孜然和小麦粉玉米饼。
Several of its signature dishes have well-documented origins.
它的几道招牌菜都有据可查的起源。
Chili con carne, a spicy stew of beef and chilies, was famously sold by "chili queens" in the plazas of San Antonio in the nineteenth century.
辣肉酱是一种用牛肉和辣椒炖成的辛辣菜，十九世纪时由“辣椒女王”们在圣安东尼奥的广场上售卖而闻名。
Nachos are said to have been invented in the 1940s by Ignacio Anaya, a restaurant worker in the border town of Piedras Negras, who improvised a snack for a group of visiting American women.
据说玉米片是二十世纪四十年代由边境小镇彼德拉斯内格拉斯的餐厅员工伊格纳西奥·阿纳亚发明的，他为一群来访的美国女士即兴做了一道小吃。
For decades, food writers dismissed Tex-Mex as an inferior imitation of "real" Mexican cooking.
几十年来，美食作家们把得州墨西哥菜贬为对“正宗”墨西哥菜的低劣模仿。
Today, it is increasingly recognized as a legitimate regional cuisine in its own right, shaped by the history of a land that was once part of Mexico.
如今，它越来越被认可为一种名正言顺的地方菜系，由这片曾属于墨西哥的土地的历史塑造而成。
q: Which ingredient does Tex-Mex use more than central Mexican food?
How has the view of Tex-Mex changed?
It is now recognized as a real regional cuisine
It is now seen as an imitation
It has been banned in Texas
It is now only eaten in Mexico

title: A Day at the Fire Station
p: Maria is a firefighter in a small American town.
玛丽亚是美国一个小镇上的消防员。
She works at the fire station for twenty-four hours and then goes home for two days.
她在消防站连续工作二十四小时，然后回家休息两天。
The firefighters eat, sleep and cook together at the station, like a big family.
消防员们在消防站一起吃饭、睡觉、做饭，就像一个大家庭。
Every morning, Maria checks the fire truck, the hoses and her heavy coat and helmet.
每天早上，玛丽亚都会检查消防车、水管以及她厚重的外套和头盔。
When the alarm rings, she must be ready to leave in about a minute.
警报一响，她必须在大约一分钟内准备好出发。
Fighting fires is only part of her job.
灭火只是她工作的一部分。
She also helps people after car accidents and teaches children what to do if there is a fire at home.
她还在车祸后帮助伤者，并教孩子们家里着火时该怎么做。
q: How long does Maria work at one time?
What does Maria check every morning?
The truck, the hoses and her coat and helmet
Which is also part of Maria's job?

title: The Zookeeper
p: Tom is a zookeeper, and his day starts at seven in the morning, before the visitors arrive.
汤姆是一名动物园饲养员，他的一天从早上七点开始，那时游客还没来。
First, he cleans the animals' homes and gives them fresh water.
首先，他打扫动物的住处，给它们换上新鲜的水。
Then he prepares their food.
然后他准备它们的食物。
The giraffes eat leaves, and the penguins eat fish.
长颈鹿吃树叶，企鹅吃鱼。
Tom watches the animals carefully every day.
汤姆每天都仔细观察动物。
If an animal does not eat or moves slowly, it may be sick, so he calls the zoo's doctor.
如果某只动物不吃东西或者行动迟缓，它可能生病了，于是他会给动物园的兽医打电话。
He also gives the animals toys and puzzles so they do not get bored.
他还给动物们玩具和益智游戏，免得它们感到无聊。
Tom says the best part of his job is getting to know each animal's personality.
汤姆说，他工作中最棒的部分是了解每只动物的个性。
q: What does Tom do if an animal does not eat?
He moves it to another zoo
Why does Tom give the animals toys?
So they do not get bored

title: Two Minutes, Twice a Day
p: Dentists say we should brush our teeth twice a day, for about two minutes each time.
牙医说，我们应该每天刷两次牙，每次大约两分钟。
Two minutes may sound short, but many people stop after only thirty or forty seconds.
两分钟听起来不长，但很多人只刷三四十秒就停下了。
Some electric toothbrushes have a timer to help.
有些电动牙刷带有计时器来帮忙。
Brushing is important because tiny bacteria live in our mouths.
刷牙很重要，因为我们的嘴里生活着微小的细菌。
They feed on sugar and make acid, and the acid can make holes in our teeth.
它们以糖为食并产生酸，而酸会在牙齿上腐蚀出洞来。
Toothpaste with fluoride helps keep teeth strong.
含氟牙膏有助于保持牙齿坚固。
It is also a good idea to visit a dentist for a checkup, even when nothing hurts.
即使牙不疼，去看牙医做个检查也是个好主意。
q: How long should we brush our teeth each time?
What makes holes in our teeth?
When should we visit a dentist?

title: Why We Need Sleep
p: We spend about one third of our lives asleep.
我们一生中大约有三分之一的时间在睡觉。
Sleep is not a waste of time.
睡觉并不是浪费时间。
While we sleep, our body repairs itself and our brain stores what we learned during the day.
我们睡觉时，身体会自我修复，大脑会储存白天学到的东西。
Teenagers usually need more sleep than adults, often eight to ten hours a night.
青少年通常比成年人需要更多睡眠，一般每晚八到十个小时。
But many students go to bed late because they are looking at their phones.
但很多学生睡得很晚，因为他们在看手机。
The bright screen can make it harder to fall asleep.
明亮的屏幕会让人更难入睡。
Doctors suggest putting the phone away before bed and going to sleep at the same time every night.
医生建议睡前把手机收起来，并且每晚在同一时间睡觉。
q: What does the brain do while we sleep?
It watches dreams on a screen
How much sleep do teenagers often need?
Putting the phone away before bed
Going to bed at different times
Looking at a screen to relax
ph: D. Sharon Pruitt, owner of Pink Sherbet PhotographyOfficial Website, www.pinksherbet.comContact Email, pink@pinksherbet.

title: Which Bin Does It Go In?
p: In many towns in the United States and the UK, families have more than one trash bin.
在美国和英国的许多城镇，每个家庭都有不止一个垃圾桶。
One is for trash, and another is for things that can be recycled, like paper, cans and some plastic bottles.
一个装普通垃圾，另一个装可回收的东西，比如纸、易拉罐和一些塑料瓶。
Some places also have a bin for food waste.
有些地方还有专门装厨余垃圾的桶。
Recycling saves materials and energy.
回收可以节约材料和能源。
For example, an old can may become part of a new can or even a bike.
比如，一个旧易拉罐可能会成为新易拉罐的一部分，甚至变成一辆自行车。
But recycling only works if people put the right things in the right bin.
但只有人们把正确的东西放进正确的桶里，回收才能起作用。
A greasy pizza box or a dirty bottle can spoil a whole load of paper or plastic, so it is best to empty and rinse containers first.
一个沾满油的披萨盒或一个脏瓶子就可能毁掉整整一车纸或塑料，所以最好先把容器倒空并冲洗干净。
q: Which of these can usually be recycled?
Food waste in the recycling bin
What can an old can become?
Part of a new can or a bike
What should you do before recycling a bottle?

title: The Animal Doctor
p: Dr. Lee is a veterinarian, or "vet," in a busy city clinic.
李医生是一名兽医，在城里一家繁忙的诊所工作。
Most of her patients are dogs and cats, but sometimes people bring rabbits, birds or even snakes.
她的病人大多是猫和狗，但有时人们也会带来兔子、鸟甚至蛇。
Her job is hard because animals cannot say where it hurts.
她的工作很难，因为动物说不出哪里疼。
She has to look, listen and ask the owners many questions.
她必须观察、倾听，并向主人问很多问题。
Is the dog eating?
狗吃东西吗？
Is the cat drinking more water than usual?
猫是不是比平时喝水更多？
She also gives young animals vaccines to protect them from dangerous diseases.
她还给幼小的动物接种疫苗，保护它们免受危险疾病的侵害。
Dr. Lee says the happiest moment is when a sick pet goes home healthy with its family.
李医生说，最开心的时刻就是生病的宠物恢复健康、和家人一起回家的时候。
q: Why is Dr. Lee's job hard?
Animals cannot say where it hurts
Who does Dr. Lee ask questions?

title: Behind the Wheel of a City Bus
p: Every weekday, Sam drives a city bus along the same route.
每个工作日，萨姆都沿着同一条路线开城市公交车。
His first trip starts at 5:30 a.m., when the streets are still dark and quiet.
他的第一趟车早上五点半出发，那时街道上还又黑又安静。
Many of his early passengers are nurses, cleaners and bakers going to work.
他早班车上的许多乘客是去上班的护士、清洁工和面包师。
Sam must keep to a timetable, but safety always comes first.
萨姆必须遵守时刻表，但安全永远是第一位的。
He waits for older people to sit down before he moves.
他会等老人坐好后才开车。
He also lowers the bus so that people in wheelchairs can get on easily.
他还会把车身降低，让坐轮椅的人能轻松上车。
After many years, Sam knows many passengers by name, and they often say "Thank you" when they get off.
多年下来，萨姆能叫出很多乘客的名字，他们下车时也常说“谢谢”。
q: When does Sam's first trip start?
What does Sam do for people in wheelchairs?
What is most important to Sam?

title: The Little Robot That Cleans
p: Many homes now have a robot vacuum.
如今很多家庭都有扫地机器人。
It is round and flat, so it can go under beds and sofas.
它又圆又扁，所以能钻到床和沙发底下。
It moves around the room by itself and picks up dust and crumbs.
它在房间里自己移动，吸起灰尘和碎屑。
The robot has sensors that help it find walls and stairs, so it does not fall down.
机器人装有传感器，帮助它发现墙壁和楼梯，这样就不会摔下去。
Some robots also make a map of the home.
有些机器人还会绘制家里的地图。
When the battery is low, the robot goes back to its base to charge.
电量不足时，机器人会回到底座充电。
However, it is not perfect.
不过，它并不完美。
Socks, cables and toys on the floor can stop it, so people still need to tidy up first!
地上的袜子、电线和玩具会把它卡住，所以人们还是得先收拾一下！
q: Why can the robot go under beds?
What does the robot do when its battery is low?
It goes back to its base
It stops in the middle of the room
Socks and cables on the floor
ph: Raysonho @ Open Grid Scheduler / Grid Engine

title: Saving in a Jar
p: When Emma was eight, her parents gave her a small allowance every week.
艾玛八岁时，父母每周给她一点零花钱。
They also gave her three glass jars with labels: Spend, Save and Share.
他们还给了她三个贴着标签的玻璃罐：“花”“存”“分享”。
Every week, Emma divided her money among the jars.
每周，艾玛都把钱分到这几个罐子里。
She used the Spend jar for snacks and stickers.
“花”罐里的钱她用来买零食和贴纸。
The Save jar was for a new bike, so it filled up slowly.
“存”罐是为了买新自行车，所以装满得很慢。
The Share jar was for giving to an animal shelter.
“分享”罐里的钱是捐给动物收容所的。
It took Emma almost a year to buy the bike, but she felt very proud.
艾玛花了将近一年才买到自行车，但她感到非常自豪。
She learned that waiting for something can make it feel even more special.
她明白了，等待一样东西会让它显得更加珍贵。
q: How many jars did Emma have?
What was the Save jar for?
Waiting can make something feel more special

title: Up Before the Sun: A Dairy Farmer
p: Jack is a dairy farmer, and his cows do not take a day off.
杰克是一名奶农，他的奶牛可从来不休息。
They need to be milked twice a day, every day of the year, even on holidays.
它们一年到头每天都要挤两次奶，节假日也不例外。
So Jack gets up at four o'clock in the morning.
所以杰克凌晨四点就起床。
Today, machines do the milking, but Jack still checks each cow.
如今挤奶由机器完成，但杰克仍然要检查每一头牛。
He makes sure they are healthy and have enough food and clean water.
他要确保它们身体健康，有足够的饲料和干净的水。
Each cow has a number tag on her ear, and some farmers use computers to follow how much milk each cow gives.
每头牛的耳朵上都有一个编号牌，有些农民还用电脑记录每头牛的产奶量。
A truck takes the milk to a factory, where it is made into milk, cheese and yogurt for the shops.
卡车把牛奶运到工厂，在那里加工成牛奶、奶酪和酸奶，送往商店。
q: How often are the cows milked?
What is on each cow's ear?

title: Eyes on the Sky
zh: 天空的守望者：空中交通管制员
p: High in a glass tower at a busy airport, Rachel watches dozens of planes take off and land.
在一个繁忙机场的玻璃塔台高处，雷切尔注视着几十架飞机起飞和降落。
She is an air traffic controller, and her job is to keep aircraft at a safe distance from one another.
她是一名空中交通管制员，她的工作是让飞机彼此之间保持安全距离。
Using radar screens and radio, she gives pilots instructions about when to land, which runway to use and how high to fly.
她借助雷达屏幕和无线电，指示飞行员何时降落、使用哪条跑道以及飞多高。
Every instruction must be clear and short, and pilots repeat it back to confirm they have understood.
每一条指令都必须简短明确，飞行员会复述一遍以确认自己听懂了。
To avoid confusion, controllers around the world use English and say numbers in a special way, such as "niner" for nine.
为了避免混淆，世界各地的管制员都使用英语，并用特殊的方式说数字，比如把九说成“niner”。
Because the work requires intense concentration, controllers take regular breaks during their shifts.
由于这项工作需要高度集中注意力，管制员在值班期间会定时休息。
Rachel admits the pressure is high, but she enjoys solving a new puzzle every few minutes.
雷切尔承认压力很大，但她享受每隔几分钟就解开一个新难题的感觉。
q: What is the main purpose of Rachel's job?
To keep aircraft at a safe distance from one another
Why do pilots repeat instructions back?
To ask for a different runway
Why do controllers take regular breaks?
They have very little to do

title: The Power of a Short Nap
p: Many people feel sleepy in the early afternoon, especially after lunch.
很多人在午后，尤其是午饭后会感到困倦。
This "afternoon dip" is a natural part of the body clock, not just the result of a heavy meal.
这种“午后低谷”是生物钟的自然组成部分，而不只是饱餐一顿的结果。
In some cultures, a midday rest has long been part of daily life.
在一些文化中，午间休息早已是日常生活的一部分。
Sleep researchers have found that a short nap of about ten to twenty minutes can improve alertness and mood.
睡眠研究者发现，大约十到二十分钟的短暂小睡可以提高警觉性、改善情绪。
The key is to wake up before the brain enters deep sleep.
关键是要在大脑进入深度睡眠之前醒来。
If a nap lasts too long, people may wake up feeling groggy, a state known as "sleep inertia."
如果小睡时间过长，人醒来时可能会昏昏沉沉，这种状态被称为“睡眠惯性”。
Napping late in the day can also make it harder to fall asleep at night.
傍晚小睡还可能让人晚上更难入睡。
For most people, then, the ideal nap is short and taken in the early afternoon.
因此，对大多数人来说，理想的小睡应该时间短，并且安排在午后早些时候。
q: According to the passage, what causes the "afternoon dip"?
How long is a good short nap?
About an hour and a half
Feeling groggy after waking from a long nap

title: The Marshmallow Test
p: In the late 1960s and early 1970s, psychologist Walter Mischel and his team at Stanford University gave young children a simple choice.
二十世纪六十年代末到七十年代初，心理学家沃尔特·米歇尔和他在斯坦福大学的团队给年幼的孩子们出了一道简单的选择题。
A child could eat one treat, such as a marshmallow, right away, or wait alone for several minutes and get two.
孩子可以马上吃掉一块零食，比如一颗棉花糖，也可以独自等上几分钟，然后得到两颗。
Some children ate the treat immediately, while others covered their eyes, sang songs or turned away to resist temptation.
有些孩子立刻就吃了，另一些则捂住眼睛、唱歌或者转过身去抵抗诱惑。
Years later, follow-up studies suggested that children who waited longer tended to do better at school.
多年后，追踪研究表明，等待时间较长的孩子往往学习成绩更好。
The test became famous as a measure of self-control.
这个实验作为衡量自控力的方法而出名。
However, more recent research with larger and more varied groups of children found that the link was weaker than first thought.
然而，近来以规模更大、背景更多样的儿童为对象的研究发现，这种关联比最初认为的要弱。
Family background, such as whether a child could trust that adults would keep their promises, also seemed to matter.
家庭背景，比如孩子是否相信大人会信守承诺，似乎也有影响。
The lesson may be that waiting is not only about willpower but also about circumstances.
也许这告诉我们，等待不仅关乎意志力，也关乎所处的环境。
q: What choice did the children have?
Eat one treat now or wait for two
Eat a treat or play a game
Sing a song or go home
Choose between a marshmallow and a cookie
What did more recent research find?
The link with school success was weaker than first thought
Waiting has no connection with anything
Children today cannot wait at all
What does the passage suggest about waiting?
It depends on both willpower and circumstances
It matters only for young children

title: Why We Put Things Off
p: Almost everyone has delayed an important task while doing something less useful, like cleaning a drawer or scrolling through videos.
几乎每个人都有过把重要任务往后推、转而去做些不那么有用的事情的经历，比如整理抽屉或刷视频。
This habit is called procrastination, and it is often blamed on laziness.
这种习惯被称为拖延，人们常常把它归咎于懒惰。
Many psychologists, however, see it differently.
然而，许多心理学家有不同的看法。
They argue that procrastination is often a way of avoiding unpleasant feelings.
他们认为，拖延往往是一种逃避不愉快情绪的方式。
A task may feel boring, confusing or frightening because we fear we will do it badly.
一项任务可能让人觉得无聊、困惑或可怕，因为我们担心自己会做不好。
Putting it off brings quick relief, but the stress returns later, usually stronger.
拖延能带来短暂的解脱，但压力过后会卷土重来，而且通常更强烈。
Some simple strategies can help.
一些简单的策略会有帮助。
Breaking a big job into small steps makes it less frightening, and promising yourself to work for just five minutes often makes starting easier.
把一项大工作分解成小步骤，会让它不那么可怕；而答应自己只干五分钟，往往能让开始变得更容易。
Being kind to yourself after a delay, rather than feeling guilty, may also reduce the chance of delaying again.
拖延之后善待自己而不是感到内疚，也可能减少再次拖延的几率。
q: According to many psychologists, what is procrastination often about?
What happens after putting a task off?
We feel relaxed for a long time
Which strategy is mentioned in the passage?
Breaking a big job into small steps

title: Tomatoes and Timers
zh: 番茄与计时器：番茄工作法
p: In the late 1980s, an Italian university student named Francesco Cirillo was struggling to focus on his studies.
二十世纪八十年代末，一位名叫弗朗切斯科·西里洛的意大利大学生在学习时很难集中注意力。
He picked up a kitchen timer shaped like a tomato and challenged himself to work without stopping until it rang.
他拿起一个番茄形状的厨房计时器，挑战自己在铃响之前一直不停地学习。
Since "pomodoro" means tomato in Italian, his method became known as the Pomodoro Technique.
由于“pomodoro”在意大利语里是番茄的意思，他的方法便被称为“番茄工作法”。
The basic idea is simple.
基本思路很简单。
You choose one task, set a timer for twenty-five minutes and work on nothing else.
你选定一项任务，设定二十五分钟的计时，期间只做这一件事。
When the timer rings, you take a short break of about five minutes, and after four rounds you take a longer one.
计时器响了，你就休息大约五分钟；完成四轮之后，再休息更长时间。
If you remember something else you need to do, you write it down and return to it later.
如果你想起别的需要做的事，就把它记下来，稍后再处理。
Supporters say the method turns a huge task into manageable pieces and makes breaks a reward rather than a distraction.
支持者说，这种方法把庞大的任务变成了可以掌控的小块，并让休息成为一种奖励而不是干扰。
q: It was invented by a farmer
How long is one work period in the method?
What should you do if you remember another task?
Write it down and return to it later

title: Working at Height: The Wind Turbine Technician
zh: 高空作业：风力发电机技术员
p: Some people go up a few floors in an elevator to get to work.
有些人坐电梯上几层楼去上班。
Carlos climbs a ladder inside a wind turbine that is taller than a thirty-story building.
卡洛斯则要在一座比三十层楼还高的风力发电机内部爬梯子。
He is a wind turbine technician, one of the jobs created by the growth of renewable energy.
他是一名风力发电机技术员，这是随着可再生能源发展而出现的职业之一。
At the top, inside a compartment called the nacelle, he inspects the gearbox, the generator and the system that turns the blades toward the wind.
在顶部一个叫做机舱的隔间里，他检查齿轮箱、发电机以及让叶片转向迎风方向的系统。
Regular maintenance prevents small faults from turning into expensive breakdowns.
定期维护可以防止小故障演变成代价高昂的大损坏。
Safety rules are strict: technicians wear harnesses, work in pairs and never climb in strong winds or thunderstorms.
安全规定很严格：技术员要系安全带、两人一组工作，并且从不在大风或雷雨天攀爬。
The job requires both technical skills and physical fitness.
这份工作既需要技术能力，也需要良好的体能。
For Carlos, the reward is the view and the knowledge that he is helping to produce clean electricity.
对卡洛斯来说，回报是那里的风景，以及知道自己正在帮助生产清洁电力。
q: Where does Carlos do much of his inspection work?
In the nacelle at the top
At the bottom of the sea
It prevents small faults from becoming expensive breakdowns
It lets technicians climb in storms
It turns the turbine off forever

title: Shrinkflation: Same Price, Less Inside
zh: 缩水式通胀：价格不变，分量变少
p: Have you ever opened a bag of chips and felt that there were fewer inside than before?
你有没有过这样的感觉：打开一袋薯片，觉得里面的量比以前少了？
You might be right.
你的感觉可能没错。
When their costs rise, some companies keep the price the same but quietly make the product smaller.
当成本上升时，有些公司保持价格不变，却悄悄把产品做小。
Economists call this "shrinkflation," a combination of "shrink" and "inflation."
经济学家称之为“缩水式通胀”，这是“缩水”和“通货膨胀”两个词的组合。
Companies do this because shoppers tend to notice a higher price much more quickly than a smaller package.
公司这样做，是因为购物者对涨价的察觉往往比对包装变小快得多。
A chocolate bar might lose a few grams, or a box of cereal might stay the same size on the outside while containing less.
一块巧克力可能少了几克，一盒麦片可能外观大小不变，里面却装得更少了。
The practice is generally legal as long as the correct weight is printed on the label.
只要标签上印着正确的重量，这种做法通常是合法的。
Consumer experts therefore advise shoppers to compare the "unit price," the cost per gram or per item, which many supermarkets display on the shelf.
因此，消费专家建议购物者比较“单价”，即每克或每件的价格，很多超市都会把它标在货架上。
q: Making a product smaller while keeping the price the same
Raising the price of a product
Why do companies prefer shrinkflation to raising prices?
Shoppers notice price increases more quickly
It is cheaper to print labels
What do experts advise shoppers to compare?

title: Phones Away at School?
p: In recent years, a growing number of schools and countries have introduced rules limiting the use of mobile phones during the school day.
近年来，越来越多的学校和国家出台规定，限制在校期间使用手机。
In some schools, students lock their phones in pouches or leave them in lockers until classes are over.
在一些学校，学生要把手机锁进专用袋里或放在储物柜里，直到放学。
Supporters believe that phones distract students from lessons and reduce face-to-face conversation during breaks.
支持者认为，手机会让学生在课堂上分心，并减少课间面对面的交流。
Teachers in schools with bans often report that playgrounds become noisier, in a good way, as students talk and play together.
实行禁令学校的老师常说，操场变得更热闹了，这是好事，因为学生们会一起聊天、玩耍。
They also hope that limiting phones will reduce online bullying.
他们还希望限制手机能减少网络欺凌。
Critics, however, point out that many parents want to contact their children in an emergency.
然而，批评者指出，很多家长希望在紧急情况下能联系上孩子。
Others argue that schools should teach young people to use technology responsibly instead of simply banning it.
还有人认为，学校应该教年轻人负责任地使用科技，而不是一禁了之。
Researchers are still studying how much difference such bans make to learning and well-being.
研究人员仍在研究此类禁令对学习和身心健康到底有多大影响。
q: What do teachers often notice in schools with phone bans?
Playgrounds become noisier as students talk and play
What is one argument against phone bans?
Parents want to contact children in an emergency
What is the current state of research on phone bans?
Researchers are still studying their effects

title: Beyond the Password
p: For decades, a password was the main thing protecting our email and bank accounts.
几十年来，密码一直是保护我们电子邮箱和银行账户的主要手段。
The problem is that passwords are easy to guess, steal or reuse.
问题在于，密码很容易被猜到、盗取或重复使用。
If you use the same password on many websites and one of them is hacked, criminals can try it everywhere.
如果你在很多网站上用同一个密码，而其中一个网站被黑客攻破，犯罪分子就可以拿它到处尝试。
That is why many services now offer two-factor authentication.
这就是为什么如今很多服务都提供双重认证。
After typing your password, you must prove your identity a second way, for example with a code sent to your phone or generated by an app.
输入密码后，你还必须用第二种方式证明身份，比如用发送到手机上的验证码或由应用程序生成的验证码。
Even if someone steals your password, they cannot log in without the second factor.
即使有人偷到了你的密码，没有第二重验证也无法登录。
Security experts also recommend using a password manager, which creates and remembers a long, unique password for every site.
安全专家还建议使用密码管理器，它会为每个网站生成并记住一个长而独特的密码。
Some companies are now moving toward "passkeys," which use your device and a fingerprint or face scan instead of a password.
一些公司正在转向“通行密钥”，用你的设备加上指纹或面部扫描来代替密码。
q: Why is reusing one password dangerous?
If one site is hacked, criminals can try it everywhere
You prove your identity a second way after the password
You call the bank every time
What does a password manager do?
Creates and remembers a unique password for every site
Removes the need for any security
ph: Tony Webster from Minneapolis, Minnesota, United States

title: Why Cities Feel Hotter
zh: 城市为什么更热：热岛效应
p: On a summer evening, the center of a big city can be noticeably warmer than the countryside around it.
在夏日傍晚，大城市的中心可能比周围的乡村明显更热。
Scientists call this the "urban heat island" effect.
科学家把这称为“城市热岛”效应。
There are several reasons for it.
造成这种现象的原因有好几个。
Dark roads and roofs absorb sunlight during the day and release the heat slowly at night.
深色的道路和屋顶白天吸收阳光，夜里再慢慢把热量释放出来。
Cars, air conditioners and factories add even more heat.
汽车、空调和工厂又增加了更多热量。
Meanwhile, cities have fewer trees and plants, which cool the air by providing shade and releasing water vapor.
与此同时，城市里的树木和植物较少，而它们能通过提供阴凉和释放水蒸气来给空气降温。
The extra heat is not just uncomfortable; during heat waves it can be dangerous, especially for elderly people.
额外的热量不仅让人不舒服，在热浪期间还可能带来危险，尤其是对老年人。
To fight it, many cities are planting more street trees, building parks and encouraging "green roofs" covered with plants.
为了应对这一问题，许多城市正在种植更多行道树、修建公园，并鼓励建设覆盖植物的“绿色屋顶”。
Some are even painting roofs and pavements in light colors to reflect sunlight.
有些城市甚至把屋顶和路面刷成浅色来反射阳光。
q: What is the "urban heat island" effect?
City centers being warmer than the countryside around them
Summer being longer in the countryside
How do trees help cool the air?
By providing shade and releasing water vapor
Why are some cities painting roofs in light colors?
To help plants grow on them

title: Paid to Find Problems: The Game Tester
zh: 找问题也是工作：游戏测试员
p: Many teenagers dream of being paid to play video games all day.
许多青少年梦想着整天玩电子游戏还能拿工资。
Game testers, also called quality assurance testers, do spend their working hours playing games, but the job is less glamorous than it sounds.
游戏测试员，也叫质量保证测试员，确实把工作时间都花在玩游戏上，但这份工作并不像听起来那么光鲜。
A tester's real task is to find bugs before the public does.
测试员真正的任务是赶在公众之前发现漏洞。
That might mean walking into the same wall a hundred times to check whether the character falls through it.
这可能意味着让角色撞同一堵墙一百次，看看他会不会穿墙掉下去。
It might also mean pressing buttons in strange orders or playing the same level for days.
也可能意味着按奇怪的顺序按键，或者连续好几天玩同一个关卡。
Every time something goes wrong, the tester writes a clear report explaining exactly how to repeat the problem, so programmers can fix it.
每当出现问题，测试员都要写一份清楚的报告，准确说明如何重现这个问题，以便程序员修复。
Patience and attention to detail matter more than being a skilled player.
耐心和对细节的关注比游戏玩得好更重要。
For some people, the job is a first step into the games industry, leading to careers in design or programming.
对一些人来说，这份工作是进入游戏行业的第一步，之后可以走向设计或编程等职业。
q: What is a game tester's real task?
To find bugs before the public does
Why does a tester write a clear report?
So programmers can repeat and fix the problem
What matters most in this job, according to the passage?

title: The Open-Plan Office
p: Walk into many modern offices and you will see long rows of desks with no walls between them.
走进许多现代办公室，你会看到一排排长长的办公桌，桌与桌之间没有任何隔断。
This open-plan design became popular because it saves space and, supposedly, encourages people to share ideas.
这种开放式设计之所以流行，是因为它节省空间，而且据说能鼓励人们交流想法。
Managers hoped that employees who could see each other would collaborate more naturally.
管理者希望，能看到彼此的员工会更自然地进行协作。
However, the reality is more complicated.
然而，现实要复杂得多。
Some studies have found that when companies moved to open offices, face-to-face conversation actually decreased while emails and messages increased.
一些研究发现，公司改用开放式办公室后，面对面的交谈反而减少了，而电子邮件和消息却增多了。
Feeling watched, many workers put on headphones to create their own private space.
由于感觉被人注视，很多员工戴上耳机，营造属于自己的私人空间。
Noise and interruptions can also make it difficult to concentrate on demanding tasks.
噪音和打扰也会让人难以专注于费脑力的工作。
As a result, many employers now mix open areas with quiet rooms and small booths for phone calls, giving staff a choice.
因此，许多雇主现在把开放区域与安静室和打电话用的小隔间结合起来，让员工有所选择。
q: Why did open-plan offices become popular?
They save space and were thought to encourage sharing ideas
They are quieter than other offices
What did some studies find after companies moved to open offices?
Mixing open areas with quiet rooms and booths

title: The Bystander Effect
p: In 1964, the murder of a young woman named Kitty Genovese in New York shocked the United States.
1964年，一位名叫基蒂·吉诺维斯的年轻女子在纽约遇害，震惊全美。
Newspapers reported that dozens of neighbors had heard or seen the attack but done nothing, although later investigations showed that this account was greatly exaggerated.
报纸报道称，有几十位邻居听到或看到了袭击却无动于衷，尽管后来的调查表明，这种说法被严重夸大了。
Nevertheless, the story inspired two psychologists, John Darley and Bibb Latané, to ask why people sometimes fail to help in emergencies.
尽管如此，这个故事还是促使两位心理学家约翰·达利和比布·拉塔内去探究：为什么人们在紧急情况下有时不施以援手。
In a series of experiments, they found that people were less likely to respond to an emergency when others were present.
在一系列实验中，他们发现，当有其他人在场时，人们对紧急情况作出反应的可能性更低。
One explanation is the "diffusion of responsibility": each person assumes that someone else will act.
一种解释是“责任分散”：每个人都以为别人会采取行动。
Another is that people look to others to decide whether a situation is serious, and if everyone appears calm, they conclude that help is unnecessary.
另一种解释是，人们会参照他人来判断情况是否严重，如果每个人看起来都很平静，他们便断定无需帮忙。
Interestingly, more recent research analyzing real public conflicts recorded on camera suggests that bystanders intervene more often than the classic studies implied.
有意思的是，近来通过分析监控录像中真实公共冲突的研究表明，旁观者出手干预的频率比经典研究所暗示的要高。
Still, the practical lesson remains valuable: if you need help in a crowd, point to one specific person and ask them directly.
不过，其中的实用经验依然很有价值：如果你在人群中需要帮助，就指向某一个具体的人，直接向他求助。
q: What did later investigations show about the newspaper reports of the Genovese case?
They underestimated the number of witnesses
Each person assumes someone else will act
People are afraid of the attacker
Only experts are responsible for helping
What practical advice does the passage give?
Ask one specific person directly for help
Wait for the crowd to leave

title: Did a Machine Write This Essay?
zh: 这篇文章是机器写的吗？
p: Since AI chatbots that can produce fluent essays in seconds became widely available, teachers around the world have faced an uncomfortable question: how can they tell whether a student's work is really the student's own?
自从能在几秒内写出流畅文章的人工智能聊天机器人普及以来，世界各地的老师都面临一个令人尴尬的问题：如何判断学生的作业是否真正出自学生本人？
Software designed to detect machine-written text has proved unreliable, sometimes flagging honest students, particularly those writing in a second language.
专门用来检测机器生成文本的软件已被证明并不可靠，有时会错误标记诚实的学生，特别是用第二语言写作的学生。
Some institutions have responded by returning to handwritten exams and oral assessments, in which students must explain their reasoning face to face.
一些院校的应对办法是重新采用手写考试和口头评估，让学生当面解释自己的思路。
Others have taken the opposite approach, arguing that banning a tool students will use throughout their careers is neither realistic nor useful.
另一些院校则采取了相反的做法，他们认为，禁止一个学生在整个职业生涯中都会使用的工具既不现实，也没有意义。
These educators redesign assignments so that students must critique an AI-generated draft, check its facts or document how they used the tool.
这些教育者重新设计作业，要求学生评析人工智能生成的初稿、核查其中的事实，或记录自己是如何使用这个工具的。
Underlying the debate is a deeper question about the purpose of writing in education.
这场争论背后是一个更深层的问题：写作在教育中的目的究竟是什么。
If an essay is merely a product to be handed in, AI makes it trivially easy to obtain.
如果文章只是一件要上交的产品，那么人工智能让它变得唾手可得。
But if writing is a way of learning to think, then outsourcing it means skipping the very process that makes education valuable.
但如果写作是学习思考的一种方式，那么把它外包出去就意味着跳过了让教育有价值的那个过程本身。
w: 轻而易举地；微不足道地
q: What problem with AI-detection software does the passage mention?
It sometimes wrongly flags honest students
It is too expensive for schools
How do some educators redesign assignments?
Students critique AI drafts or check their facts
Students must write without computers at home
According to the final paragraph, why might outsourcing writing be harmful?
Writing is a way of learning to think

title: When Antibiotics Stop Working
p: When Alexander Fleming noticed in 1928 that a mold had killed bacteria in one of his petri dishes, he opened the door to one of medicine's greatest achievements.
1928年，亚历山大·弗莱明注意到一种霉菌杀死了他培养皿里的细菌，由此打开了医学史上最伟大成就之一的大门。
Penicillin and the antibiotics that followed turned once-deadly infections into routine illnesses.
青霉素以及随后出现的各种抗生素，把曾经致命的感染变成了寻常小病。
Yet in his Nobel Prize speech in 1945, Fleming warned that misuse of the drug could allow bacteria to become resistant.
然而，弗莱明在1945年的诺贝尔奖演讲中就警告说，滥用这种药物可能会让细菌产生耐药性。
His warning proved accurate.
他的警告后来被证明是准确的。
Whenever an antibiotic is used, the most vulnerable bacteria die first, while any that happen to survive can multiply and pass on their resistance.
每当使用抗生素时，最脆弱的细菌最先死亡，而碰巧存活下来的细菌则会繁殖并把耐药性传下去。
Taking antibiotics for viral infections such as colds, which they cannot treat, or stopping a course early, gives this process more opportunities.
用抗生素治疗它们根本治不了的病毒感染（如感冒），或者提前停药，都为这一过程提供了更多机会。
The heavy use of antibiotics in farm animals adds to the problem.
在养殖动物身上大量使用抗生素更是加剧了这一问题。
The World Health Organization regards antimicrobial resistance as one of the top global threats to public health.
世界卫生组织将抗微生物药物耐药性视为全球公共卫生面临的最大威胁之一。
Solutions include developing new drugs, improving hygiene and vaccination to prevent infections in the first place, and prescribing antibiotics only when they are genuinely needed.
解决办法包括研发新药、改善卫生条件和推广疫苗接种以从源头上预防感染，以及仅在真正需要时才开具抗生素。
q: What did Fleming warn about in 1945?
Why is taking antibiotics for a cold a problem?
They cannot treat viral infections and encourage resistance
It makes the cold last forever
Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a solution?
Using more antibiotics in farm animals

title: Four Days a Week?
p: The idea of a five-day, forty-hour working week is so familiar that it seems almost natural, yet it is a relatively recent invention.
每周工作五天、四十小时的观念如此熟悉，以至于看起来几乎是天经地义的，但它其实是相对较新的发明。
In the 1920s, the American industrialist Henry Ford adopted it in his factories, partly in the belief that workers with more leisure time would also buy more goods.
二十世纪二十年代，美国实业家亨利·福特在他的工厂里采用了这一制度，部分原因是他相信，有更多闲暇时间的工人也会购买更多商品。
Today, some companies are experimenting with a further step: a four-day week without a cut in pay.
如今，一些公司正在尝试更进一步：每周工作四天，而工资不减。

In trials in several countries, including a large pilot in the UK in 2022, many participating employers reported that productivity held steady while staff felt less stressed and were less likely to quit.
在包括2022年英国一项大型试点在内的多个国家的试验中，许多参与的雇主表示，生产率保持稳定，而员工的压力减轻，离职意愿也降低了。
The secret, supporters say, is cutting unnecessary meetings and distractions rather than simply squeezing five days of work into four.
支持者说，秘诀在于砍掉不必要的会议和干扰，而不是简单地把五天的工作塞进四天。
Skeptics point out that the companies volunteering for such trials may be those best suited to them.
怀疑者指出，自愿参加这类试验的公司可能本来就是最适合这种模式的公司。
It is far from clear how a shorter week would work for hospitals, schools or shops that must stay open, and some employees find longer working days exhausting.
对于必须保持开放的医院、学校或商店来说，缩短工作周如何实施还远不清楚，而且一些员工觉得更长的工作日令人筋疲力尽。
q: Why did Henry Ford partly support a shorter week?
He believed workers with more leisure would buy more goods
He wanted to close his factories
Workers refused to work on Saturdays
According to supporters, what is the secret to a successful four-day week?
Companies that volunteer may be the ones best suited to it
Workers will earn too much money

title: The Gentle Power of the Nudge
p: Traditional economics assumed that people make rational decisions by carefully weighing costs and benefits.
传统经济学假定，人们会通过仔细权衡成本和收益来做出理性的决定。
Behavioral economists, however, have shown that our choices are strongly influenced by how options are presented.
然而，行为经济学家已经证明，我们的选择在很大程度上受到选项呈现方式的影响。
In their 2008 book Nudge, Richard Thaler and Cass Sunstein argued that governments and organizations could use this insight to help people make better decisions without restricting their freedom.
理查德·塞勒和卡斯·桑斯坦在2008年出版的《助推》一书中提出，政府和组织可以利用这一洞见，在不限制人们自由的前提下帮助他们做出更好的决定。
Thaler later received the Nobel Prize in Economics in 2017.
塞勒后来于2017年获得了诺贝尔经济学奖。
A classic example is the power of defaults.
一个经典的例子是默认选项的力量。
When employees are automatically enrolled in a retirement savings plan and must actively choose to leave it, far more of them end up saving than when they must actively sign up.
如果员工被自动加入退休储蓄计划，必须主动选择才能退出，那么最终存钱的人数会比必须主动报名时多得多。
Similarly, placing fruit at eye level in a cafeteria can encourage healthier eating without banning anything.
同样，在食堂里把水果放在与视线齐平的位置，可以在不禁止任何东西的情况下鼓励更健康的饮食。
Critics worry that nudges can be manipulative, especially when companies use the same techniques to push customers toward choices that benefit the company rather than the customer.
批评者担心助推可能带有操纵性，尤其是当企业用同样的手段把顾客推向有利于企业而非顾客的选择时。
Supporters respond that every choice is presented in some way, so the real question is whether the design serves people's own interests.
支持者回应说，任何选择都必然以某种方式呈现，所以真正的问题在于这种设计是否符合人们自身的利益。
q: People make rational decisions by weighing costs and benefits
People's choices depend on how options are presented
Why do more employees save when enrolled automatically?
Because of the power of defaults
Because saving is required by law
Because they read the plan carefully
What is the critics' main concern about nudges?

title: Fast Fashion's Hidden Costs
p: Not long ago, most clothing brands released new collections a few times a year.
不久以前，大多数服装品牌一年只推出几次新系列。
Today, so-called fast fashion companies can move a design from the drawing board to the store in a matter of weeks, offering cheap, trendy clothes that many shoppers wear only a handful of times.
如今，所谓的快时尚公司能在短短几周内把一个设计从画板送进门店，提供廉价而时髦的衣服，而很多购物者只穿几次就不穿了。
The low price tag, however, conceals considerable costs.
然而，低廉的价签背后隐藏着相当大的代价。
Growing cotton requires large amounts of water, and dyeing fabric can pollute rivers when factories release untreated wastewater.
种植棉花需要大量的水，而如果工厂排放未经处理的废水，布料染色还可能污染河流。
Many cheap garments are made from polyester, a plastic-based material that sheds tiny fibers when washed.
许多廉价服装由涤纶制成，这是一种以塑料为原料的材料，洗涤时会脱落微小的纤维。
The human cost drew worldwide attention in 2013, when the Rana Plaza building in Bangladesh, which housed several garment factories, collapsed and killed more than a thousand workers.
2013年，孟加拉国容纳了数家服装厂的拉纳广场大楼倒塌，造成一千多名工人死亡，其中的人力代价由此引起全世界关注。
In response, some consumers are buying second-hand, repairing clothes or simply buying less.
作为回应，一些消费者开始购买二手衣物、修补衣服，或者干脆少买。
Some brands now offer repair services or take back old clothes, although critics warn that such schemes can be little more than marketing unless overall production falls.
一些品牌现在提供修补服务或回收旧衣，不过批评者警告说，除非总产量下降，否则这类计划可能只不过是营销手段而已。
q: What is typical of fast fashion companies?
They move designs to stores within weeks
They release one collection every few years
They make clothes to last a lifetime
What problem with polyester does the passage mention?
It sheds tiny fibers when washed
It needs huge amounts of water to grow
Why are critics skeptical of take-back schemes?
They may be just marketing unless overall production falls
They are illegal in many countries

title: Inside the Filter Bubble
p: Every time you like a post, watch a video to the end or click on a headline, you are teaching an algorithm what you prefer.
每当你点赞一条帖子、看完一个视频或点开一条新闻标题，你都在教算法了解你的喜好。
Social media platforms and video sites use this information to recommend more content you are likely to enjoy, which keeps you on the platform longer.
社交媒体平台和视频网站利用这些信息，向你推荐更多你可能喜欢的内容，从而让你在平台上停留更久。
In 2011, the internet activist Eli Pariser coined the term "filter bubble" to describe a possible side effect of this personalization.
2011年，网络活动人士伊莱·帕里泽创造了“过滤气泡”一词，用来描述这种个性化推荐可能带来的副作用。
If we mainly see information that matches our existing views, he argued, we may gradually lose contact with other perspectives and become more certain that we are right.
他认为，如果我们看到的主要是与自己既有观点相符的信息，我们可能会逐渐与其他视角失去接触，并变得更加确信自己是对的。
Researchers continue to debate how strong this effect really is.
研究人员对于这种效应到底有多强仍有争议。
Some studies suggest that many people still encounter a range of viewpoints online, and that our own choices about whom to follow may matter as much as any algorithm.
一些研究表明，很多人在网上仍会接触到各种不同的观点，而我们自己选择关注谁，可能与任何算法一样重要。
Even so, the concept has encouraged a healthy habit: deliberately seeking out reliable sources that challenge, rather than simply confirm, what we already believe.
即便如此，这一概念还是促成了一个健康的习惯：有意识地寻找那些挑战而不是单纯印证我们已有观念的可靠信息来源。
q: Why do platforms recommend content you are likely to enjoy?
To keep you on the platform longer
Mainly seeing information that matches your existing views
A way to clean your phone screen
A type of social media platform
Our own choices of whom to follow may matter as much as algorithms
Filter bubbles do not exist at all

title: The Puzzle of the Placebo
p: A placebo is a treatment with no active ingredient, such as a sugar pill, yet patients who take one sometimes report genuine improvement.
安慰剂是一种不含有效成分的治疗手段，比如糖丸，然而服用它的病人有时会报告病情确实有所好转。
This placebo effect is especially noticeable for symptoms such as pain, nausea and fatigue, which are strongly shaped by the brain's expectations.
这种安慰剂效应在疼痛、恶心和疲劳等症状上尤为明显，因为这些症状在很大程度上受大脑预期的影响。
Because of it, new medicines are usually tested in randomized, double-blind trials.
正因如此，新药通常要经过随机双盲试验的检验。
One group receives the real drug and another receives an identical-looking placebo, and neither the patients nor the researchers know who received which until the end.
一组服用真药，另一组服用外观相同的安慰剂，直到试验结束，病人和研究人员都不知道谁服用的是哪一种。
A drug is considered effective only if it performs clearly better than the placebo.
只有当药物的效果明显好于安慰剂时，它才被认为是有效的。
Surprisingly, some studies have found that placebos can help even when patients are told openly that the pills contain nothing active.
令人惊讶的是，一些研究发现，即使明确告诉病人药片里不含任何有效成分，安慰剂仍然可能起作用。
Researchers believe the ritual of care, including a confident doctor, a clear explanation and the act of taking medicine, may trigger the body's own pain-relieving systems.
研究人员认为，包括一位自信的医生、清楚的解释以及服药这一行为在内的整个关怀仪式，可能会激活人体自身的镇痛系统。
Placebos cannot shrink tumors or cure infections, but they remind us that the relationship between mind and body is more intricate than we once thought.
安慰剂无法让肿瘤缩小或治愈感染，但它们提醒我们，身心之间的关系比我们曾经以为的要复杂得多。
q: For which kind of symptoms is the placebo effect especially noticeable?
In a double-blind trial, who knows which patients receive the real drug?
No one, until the end of the trial
Placebos can help even when patients know they are placebos
Placebos work better than all real drugs

title: Old Faithful
p: Yellowstone became the world's first national park in 1872.
黄石在1872年成为世界上第一个国家公园。
Most of the park is in the state of Wyoming.
公园的大部分位于怀俄明州。
Under the ground, there is very hot rock, so the water there gets hot too.
地下有非常炽热的岩石，所以那里的水也会变热。
Old Faithful is the park's most famous geyser.
老忠实泉是公园里最有名的间歇泉。
About every hour and a half, it shoots hot water and steam high into the air.
大约每隔一个半小时，它就会把热水和蒸汽高高地喷向空中。
Park rangers can guess the next time, so visitors sit and wait with their cameras.
公园管理员能预测下一次喷发的时间，所以游客们拿着相机坐着等待。
While they wait, they may also see big brown bison walking near the road.
等待的时候，他们还可能看到棕色的大野牛在路边走动。
q: When did Yellowstone become a national park?
How often does Old Faithful erupt?
About every hour and a half
What animal might visitors see near the road?

title: The Lady in the Harbor
p: The Statue of Liberty stands on a small island in New York Harbor.
自由女神像矗立在纽约港的一座小岛上。
It was a gift from the people of France to the United States.
它是法国人民送给美国的礼物。
It opened in 1886.
它于1886年落成。
The statue is made of copper.
这座雕像是用铜做的。
At first it was a shiny brown color, but over the years the air and rain turned it green.
起初它是闪亮的棕色，但多年来空气和雨水把它变成了绿色。
In her right hand, the lady holds a torch.
女神右手举着一支火炬。
In her left hand, she holds a tablet with the date July 4, 1776.
她左手拿着一块写着1776年7月4日的书板。
For many people who came to America by ship, she was their first view of their new home.
对于许多乘船来到美国的人来说，她是他们看到新家园的第一眼。
q: Who gave the statue to the United States?
Why is the statue green today?
Air and rain changed the copper
It is made of green stone
What does the statue hold in her right hand?

title: Who Is Big Ben?
p: Many visitors to London want to see Big Ben.
许多去伦敦的游客都想看看大本钟。
They usually point at the tall clock tower next to the River Thames.
他们通常会指着泰晤士河边那座高高的钟楼。
But Big Ben is really the name of the huge bell inside the tower!
但其实“大本”是钟楼里那口巨大的钟的名字！
The tower has its own name, too.
这座塔也有自己的名字。
In 2012, it was named the Elizabeth Tower for Queen Elizabeth II.
2012年，它为纪念女王伊丽莎白二世而被命名为伊丽莎白塔。
The clock has four faces, so people can read the time from every side.
这座钟有四个钟面，所以人们从各个方向都能看到时间。
Every hour, the great bell rings with a deep BONG.
每到整点，大钟就会发出低沉的“咚”声。
People all over Britain listen to it on the radio on New Year's Eve.
新年前夜，全英国的人都会在收音机里听它的钟声。
q: What is "Big Ben" really the name of?
What is the tower called now?
How many faces does the clock have?

title: Hop, Hop, Kangaroo
p: Kangaroos live only in Australia and nearby islands.
袋鼠只生活在澳大利亚及附近的岛屿上。
They have strong back legs and a long, heavy tail.
它们有强壮的后腿和一条又长又重的尾巴。
They do not walk like us; they hop, and they can move very fast.
它们不像我们那样走路，而是跳着走，而且速度非常快。
The tail helps them keep their balance.
尾巴帮助它们保持平衡。
A baby kangaroo is called a joey.
小袋鼠叫作 joey。
When it is born, it is as small as a bean.
它刚出生时只有一粒豆子那么小。
It lives in its mother's pouch and drinks her milk for months.
它住在妈妈的育儿袋里，喝妈妈的奶，一住就是好几个月。
In Australia, you can see yellow road signs with a kangaroo on them, because the animals often cross the road.
在澳大利亚，你能看到画着袋鼠的黄色路标，因为这种动物经常横穿马路。
q: What is a baby kangaroo called?
Why are there kangaroo road signs in Australia?

title: Teddy's Bear
p: Theodore Roosevelt was president of the United States from 1901 to 1909.
西奥多·罗斯福在1901年至1909年间担任美国总统。
His nickname was "Teddy."
他的昵称是“泰迪”。
In 1902, he went on a bear hunt in Mississippi.
1902年，他去密西西比州猎熊。
Some men tied a tired old bear to a tree and asked him to shoot it, but he said no.
有人把一头疲惫的老熊绑在树上，让他开枪，但他拒绝了。
A newspaper printed a funny drawing of the story.
一家报纸刊登了一幅关于这件事的有趣漫画。
Soon after, a shop owner in New York made a soft toy bear and called it "Teddy's bear."
不久之后，纽约的一位店主做了一只柔软的玩具熊，取名“泰迪的熊”。
The toy became very popular.
这种玩具变得非常受欢迎。
Today, children all over the world sleep with their teddy bears.
如今，全世界的孩子都抱着泰迪熊睡觉。
q: What did Roosevelt do when he saw the tied bear?
Who made the first "Teddy's bear" in this story?
A shop owner in New York

title: The Stones on the Plain
p: Stonehenge is a circle of giant stones in the south of England.
巨石阵是英格兰南部的一圈巨大石头。
People started to build it about 5,000 years ago.
人们大约在5000年前开始建造它。
Some of the stones are taller than two men, and they are very heavy.
有些石头比两个人还高，而且非常沉重。
Many of the smaller stones came from Wales, more than 200 kilometers away.
许多较小的石头来自威尔士，距离这里200多公里。
There were no trucks or machines then, so how did people move them?
那时没有卡车或机器，人们是怎么搬动它们的呢？
Nobody knows for sure.
没有人确切知道。
We do know that the stones line up with the sun.
但我们知道，这些石头与太阳的位置对齐。
On the longest day of summer, many people come to watch the sun rise over the stones.
在夏天白昼最长的那一天，许多人会来看太阳从石头上方升起。
q: When did people start building Stonehenge?
Where did the smaller stones come from?
When do many people come to watch the sunrise there?
On the longest day of summer
On the coldest night of winter

title: A Green Day in March
p: March 17 is St. Patrick's Day.
3月17日是圣帕特里克节。
St. Patrick is the patron saint of Ireland.
圣帕特里克是爱尔兰的守护圣人。
On this day, people in Ireland and many other countries wear green clothes.
在这一天，爱尔兰和其他许多国家的人都穿绿色的衣服。
Some people wear a shamrock, a small plant with three leaves.
有些人会佩戴三叶草，一种长着三片叶子的小植物。
There are big parades with music and dancing in Dublin, New York and other cities.
在都柏林、纽约和其他城市都有带着音乐和舞蹈的盛大游行。
In Chicago, workers even make the river bright green for the day!
在芝加哥，工人们甚至会在这一天把河水染成鲜绿色！
Many Americans have Irish families from long ago, so the day is very popular in the United States, too.
许多美国人的祖上来自爱尔兰，所以这个节日在美国也很受欢迎。
q: How many leaves does a shamrock have?
What happens to the river in Chicago?

title: Will Winter End Soon?
p: February 2 is Groundhog Day in the United States and Canada.
2月2日是美国和加拿大的土拨鼠日。
A groundhog is a furry brown animal that sleeps under the ground all winter.
土拨鼠是一种毛茸茸的棕色动物，整个冬天都在地下睡觉。
An old story says it can tell us when spring will come.
一个古老的说法认为，它能告诉我们春天什么时候到来。
The most famous groundhog is Punxsutawney Phil, from a small town in Pennsylvania.
最有名的土拨鼠是来自宾夕法尼亚州一个小镇的旁苏托尼·菲尔。
Early in the morning, thousands of people wait in the cold to see him come out.
清晨，成千上万的人在寒冷中等着看它出洞。
If Phil sees his shadow, there will be six more weeks of winter.
如果菲尔看到了自己的影子，冬天就还要持续六个星期。
If he does not, spring will come early.
如果没看到，春天就会提前到来。
Of course, he is not always right, but everyone has fun!
当然，它并不总是猜对，但大家都玩得很开心！
q: Where does Punxsutawney Phil come from?
What does it mean if Phil sees his shadow?
ph: Anthony Quintano from Mount Laurel, United States

title: The Orange Bridge in the Fog
p: The Golden Gate Bridge is in San Francisco, California.
金门大桥位于加利福尼亚州旧金山。
It opened in 1937.
它于1937年通车。
At that time, it was the longest bridge of its kind in the world.
在当时，它是世界上同类桥梁中最长的。
Its name is "golden," but the bridge is not gold at all.
它的名字里有“金”字，但这座桥根本不是金色的。
Its color is called "International Orange."
它的颜色叫作“国际橙”。
This color is easy to see, and it looks beautiful next to the blue sea and green hills.
这种颜色很醒目，在蓝色大海和绿色山丘的映衬下非常漂亮。
In summer, thick fog often covers the bridge, and sometimes only the tops of its two towers can be seen.
夏天，浓雾经常笼罩大桥，有时只能看见两座桥塔的塔顶。
You can walk or ride a bike across it.
你可以步行或骑自行车过桥。
q: What color is the Golden Gate Bridge?
What often covers the bridge in summer?

title: The Bird That Cannot Fly
p: The kiwi is a small brown bird from New Zealand.
几维鸟是一种来自新西兰的棕色小鸟。
It has wings, but they are very small, and it cannot fly.
它有翅膀，但翅膀非常小，所以它不会飞。
It sleeps in the day and looks for food at night.
它白天睡觉，晚上出来找食物。
The kiwi has a long beak with its nose at the very end.
几维鸟有一个长长的喙，鼻孔就长在喙的最尖端。
It pushes its beak into the ground and smells worms and insects.
它把喙插进泥土里，嗅出蠕虫和昆虫。
The mother lays a very big egg for her size.
按体型来说，鸟妈妈产下的蛋非常大。
The kiwi is a national symbol, and people from New Zealand often call themselves "Kiwis."
几维鸟是国家象征，新西兰人也常常称自己为“Kiwi”。
q: When does the kiwi look for food?
At the end of its beak
What do people from New Zealand often call themselves?

title: Reading the Grand Canyon
p: Standing at the edge of the Grand Canyon in Arizona, many visitors simply fall silent.
站在亚利桑那州大峡谷的边缘，许多游客会不由得沉默下来。
The canyon is about 446 kilometers long and, in places, more than 1.6 kilometers deep.
这条峡谷长约446公里，有些地方深达1.6公里以上。
It was carved over millions of years by the Colorado River, which still flows along the bottom.
它是由科罗拉多河在数百万年间切割而成的，这条河至今仍在谷底流淌。
To geologists, the canyon walls are like the pages of a giant history book.
在地质学家眼里，峡谷的岩壁就像一本巨大历史书的书页。
Each colored layer of rock was formed in a different period, and the oldest rocks at the bottom are nearly two billion years old.
每一层彩色岩石都形成于不同时期，谷底最古老的岩石已有近20亿年历史。
Fossils of sea creatures in the upper layers show that this dry land was once covered by water.
上层岩石中的海洋生物化石表明，这片干燥的土地曾经被海水覆盖。
The canyon became a national park in 1919, and today millions of people visit each year.
大峡谷于1919年成为国家公园，如今每年有数百万人到访。
Rangers warn hikers that walking down is easy but climbing back up in the summer heat can be dangerous, so they should carry plenty of water.
管理员提醒徒步者，下坡容易，但在夏日酷热中爬回来可能很危险，因此要带足水。
q: What do the sea fossils in the rocks show?
The land was once under water
Fish still live in the walls
The river used to be salty
What do rangers advise hikers to do?

title: Twelve Seconds at Kitty Hawk
p: Orville and Wilbur Wright never finished college, yet they solved one of the greatest puzzles of their time.
奥维尔和威尔伯·莱特兄弟从未读完大学，却解开了他们那个时代最大的难题之一。
The brothers ran a bicycle shop in Dayton, Ohio, and the money from selling and repairing bikes paid for their experiments.
兄弟俩在俄亥俄州代顿开了一家自行车店，靠卖车和修车赚的钱来支付他们的实验费用。
Working with bicycles also taught them that a rider stays up by constantly balancing, an idea they applied to controlling an aircraft.
和自行车打交道还让他们明白，骑车人是靠不断保持平衡才不会倒下的，他们把这个想法用在了控制飞机上。
They tested their gliders on the windy sand hills near Kitty Hawk, North Carolina.
他们在北卡罗来纳州基蒂霍克附近多风的沙丘上测试滑翔机。
When published data on wings turned out to be wrong, they built their own small wind tunnel and collected new measurements.
当他们发现已发表的机翼数据有误时，就自己造了一个小风洞，重新测量数据。
On December 17, 1903, Orville lay on the lower wing of their engine-powered Flyer and took off.
1903年12月17日，奥维尔趴在他们那架装有发动机的“飞行者号”的下层机翼上起飞了。
The flight lasted just 12 seconds and covered about 37 meters, less than the length of a modern passenger jet.
那次飞行只持续了12秒，飞了大约37米，比一架现代客机的机身还短。
Wilbur flew 59 seconds later that day, and the age of powered flight had begun.
当天晚些时候，威尔伯飞了59秒，动力飞行的时代就此开始。
q: How did the Wright brothers pay for their experiments?
With money from their bicycle shop
With prize money from a contest
Why did they build a wind tunnel?
Published wing data turned out to be wrong
They were asked to by a newspaper
How long did the first flight on December 17, 1903 last?

title: All the World's a Stage
p: In 1599, an acting company that included William Shakespeare built a theater called the Globe on the south bank of the River Thames.
1599年，莎士比亚所在的一个剧团在泰晤士河南岸建了一座名为“环球”的剧院。
Many of his greatest plays, including Hamlet and Macbeth, were first performed there.
他的许多伟大剧作，包括《哈姆雷特》和《麦克白》，都是在那里首演的。
The theater was open to the sky, so performances took place in the afternoon, using daylight.
剧院是露天的，所以演出都在下午进行，借助日光照明。
Tickets were cheap for "groundlings," who stood in the yard right in front of the stage.
站在舞台正前方空地上的“站票观众”票价很便宜。
They ate, drank and shouted at the actors, making the experience far noisier than a modern evening at the theater.
他们边吃边喝，还冲着演员喊叫，使看戏的体验比现代剧院的晚场热闹得多。
In 1613, a cannon fired during a play set fire to the thatched roof, and the building burned down within an hour.
1613年，一场演出中发射的炮火点燃了茅草屋顶，整座建筑在一小时内被烧毁。
A careful reconstruction, Shakespeare's Globe, opened near the original site in 1997.
1997年，一座经过精心复原的“莎士比亚环球剧院”在原址附近开放。
It was the first building allowed to have a thatched roof in London since the Great Fire of 1666, and audiences can still buy standing tickets today.
它是自1666年伦敦大火以来第一座获准使用茅草屋顶的伦敦建筑，如今观众仍然可以买站票。
q: Why were plays at the original Globe performed in the afternoon?
What destroyed the first Globe in 1613?
A fire started by a cannon
What is special about the modern Globe's roof?

It can be opened and closed

title: Born in New Orleans
p: Many people call New Orleans, Louisiana, the birthplace of jazz.
许多人称路易斯安那州的新奥尔良为爵士乐的发源地。
In the 1800s, the port city was a mix of African, French, Spanish and Caribbean cultures.
19世纪，这座港口城市融合了非洲、法国、西班牙和加勒比的文化。
On Sundays, enslaved Africans gathered in a place called Congo Square to play drums, sing and dance, keeping their musical traditions alive.
每逢周日，被奴役的非洲人会聚集在一个叫“刚果广场”的地方打鼓、唱歌、跳舞，使自己的音乐传统得以延续。
By the early 1900s, local brass bands were mixing blues, church music and marching songs into something new.
到了20世纪初，当地的铜管乐队把布鲁斯、教堂音乐和进行曲融合成了一种新的音乐。
Musicians often improvised, inventing melodies on the spot instead of reading every note from paper.
乐手们经常即兴演奏，当场创作旋律，而不是照着乐谱演奏每一个音符。
Louis Armstrong, who grew up poor in the city, became one of the most famous trumpet players in history.
在这座城市的贫困环境中长大的路易斯·阿姆斯特朗，成为了史上最著名的小号手之一。
Jazz is still part of daily life there.
爵士乐至今仍是当地日常生活的一部分。
At some funerals, a brass band plays slow, sad music on the way to the cemetery and joyful tunes on the way back, as people dance in the street behind it.
在一些葬礼上，铜管乐队去墓地的路上演奏缓慢悲伤的音乐，回来时则演奏欢快的曲调，人们跟在后面在街上跳舞。
q: What happened in Congo Square on Sundays?
Enslaved Africans played music and danced
What does it mean that jazz musicians improvised?
They invented melodies on the spot
They read every note from paper
How does the music change at some New Orleans funerals?
It is sad going to the cemetery and joyful coming back
It is joyful the whole time
There is no music at all
It gets slower on the way back

title: A Garden Under the Sea
p: Off the coast of Queensland, in northeastern Australia, lies the Great Barrier Reef.
在澳大利亚东北部昆士兰州的海岸外，坐落着大堡礁。
It stretches for more than 2,300 kilometers and is made up of about 2,900 separate reefs.
它绵延2300多公里，由大约2900个独立的礁体组成。
It is often called the largest structure on Earth built by living things.
它常被称为地球上由生物建造的最大结构。
Those builders are tiny animals called coral polyps.
这些建造者是一种叫作珊瑚虫的微小动物。
Each polyp makes a hard skeleton, and over thousands of years, countless skeletons pile up to form reefs.
每只珊瑚虫都会形成坚硬的骨骼，经过数千年，无数骨骼堆积起来形成了礁体。
The reef provides a home for thousands of species, from colorful fish to sea turtles and sharks.
这片珊瑚礁为成千上万的物种提供了家园，从色彩斑斓的鱼到海龟和鲨鱼。
However, the reef is under threat.
然而，这片珊瑚礁正面临威胁。
When the ocean becomes too warm, corals push out the tiny algae that live inside them and give them color, a process known as bleaching.
海水过热时，珊瑚会排出生活在体内、赋予它们颜色的微小藻类，这一过程被称为白化。
Bleached corals can recover if the water cools, but repeated heat waves make that harder, so scientists are watching the reef closely.
如果海水降温，白化的珊瑚可以恢复，但反复的热浪让恢复越来越难，所以科学家们正密切关注这片珊瑚礁。
q: What builds the Great Barrier Reef?
Ocean water that is too warm
According to the article, can bleached corals recover?

title: The Festival Nobody Invited
p: Every August, the Scottish capital of Edinburgh fills with comedians, actors, dancers and musicians from around the world.
每年八月，苏格兰首府爱丁堡都会挤满来自世界各地的喜剧演员、演员、舞者和音乐人。
They come for the Edinburgh Festival Fringe, often described as the largest arts festival on the planet.
他们是为爱丁堡艺穗节而来的，这个节日常被称为全世界规模最大的艺术节。
The Fringe began almost by accident.
艺穗节的诞生几乎是个意外。
In 1947, a new international festival was launched in the city, but eight theater groups that had not been invited turned up anyway.
1947年，这座城市创办了一个新的国际艺术节，但有八个没有受到邀请的剧团还是来了。
They performed on the "fringe," or edge, of the official event, and the name stuck.
他们在官方活动的“边缘”演出，这个名字从此就沿用了下来。
Its key rule is still that anyone with a show and a venue can take part; there is no committee that selects performers.
它最重要的规则至今仍是：只要有节目、有场地，任何人都能参加；没有委员会来挑选演员。
As a result, you might see a famous comedian in a large theater and then a student play in a tiny room above a pub on the same day.
因此，你可能同一天里既在大剧院看到知名喜剧演员，又在酒吧楼上的小房间里看到学生演的戏。
On the Royal Mile, the city's old main street, performers hand out flyers and put on free shows to attract audiences.
在城市古老的主街皇家英里大道上，表演者们派发传单、免费表演来吸引观众。
w: （名称）沿用下来（stick 的过去式）
q: The Queen ordered a new festival
A pub owner held a contest
Who can perform at the Fringe?
Anyone with a show and a venue
Only groups chosen by a committee
What do performers do on the Royal Mile?
Hand out flyers and give free shows

title: At the Edge of an Empire
p: Nearly 1,900 years ago, the Roman Emperor Hadrian ordered a wall to be built across northern Britain.
大约1900年前，罗马皇帝哈德良下令在不列颠北部修建一道城墙。
Construction began around AD 122, and the wall ran about 117 kilometers from coast to coast.
工程大约在公元122年开始，城墙从一侧海岸延伸到另一侧海岸，长约117公里。
Small forts were placed roughly every Roman mile, with larger forts holding hundreds of soldiers.
大约每隔一罗马里就设有一座小堡垒，较大的要塞则能驻扎数百名士兵。
Historians still debate its exact purpose.
历史学家对它的确切用途仍有争论。
It may have been less a barrier for battle than a way to control movement and collect taxes on trade.
与其说它是作战的屏障，不如说它可能是用来控制人员往来和对贸易征税的。
Some of the most surprising discoveries came from Vindolanda, a fort just south of the wall.
一些最令人惊讶的发现来自哈德良长城以南不远的文德兰达要塞。
There, archaeologists found thin wooden tablets with handwritten letters, including a birthday party invitation from one officer's wife to another woman.
考古学家在那里发现了写有手写信件的薄木片，其中包括一位军官的妻子写给另一位女士的生日聚会邀请。
Today, walkers can follow a long-distance trail beside the wall's remains, which became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1987.
如今，徒步者可以沿着长城遗迹旁的长途步道行走，这处遗迹在1987年被列入联合国教科文组织世界遗产名录。
q: Who ordered the wall to be built?
According to historians, what might the wall have been used for?

title: Two Fathoms Deep
p: Samuel Clemens grew up in Hannibal, Missouri, a small town on the banks of the Mississippi River.
塞缪尔·克莱门斯在密苏里州汉尼拔长大，那是密西西比河畔的一座小镇。
As a boy, he watched the great steamboats arrive and dreamed of working on one.
小时候，他看着巨大的蒸汽船靠岸，梦想着能在船上工作。
As a young man, he made that dream come true and trained as a riverboat pilot.
年轻时，他实现了这个梦想，接受训练成为一名内河船领航员。
On the river, crew members measured the depth of the water and called out the results.
在河上，船员们会测量水深并大声报出结果。
"Mark twain!" meant two fathoms, about 3.7 meters — deep enough for a boat to pass safely.
“Mark twain！”意思是两英寻，大约3.7米——足够船只安全通过的深度。
Clemens later chose this call as his pen name.
克莱门斯后来选用这句喊声作为自己的笔名。
As Mark Twain, he wrote The Adventures of Tom Sawyer and Adventures of Huckleberry Finn, drawing on memories of his river childhood.
他以马克·吐温之名写下了《汤姆·索亚历险记》和《哈克贝利·费恩历险记》，书中取材于他在河边度过的童年记忆。
His humor and his use of everyday American speech helped shape modern American literature.
他的幽默和对美国日常口语的运用，帮助塑造了现代美国文学。
q: What job did Samuel Clemens train for as a young man?
What did the call "Mark twain!" mean?
The water was two fathoms deep
Where did Twain get material for Tom Sawyer and Huckleberry Finn?
His memories of growing up by the river

title: "Mr. Watson, Come Here"
p: Alexander Graham Bell was born in Edinburgh, Scotland, in 1847, into a family fascinated by speech and sound.
亚历山大·格雷厄姆·贝尔1847年出生于苏格兰爱丁堡，他的家人都对语言和声音充满兴趣。
His mother gradually lost her hearing, and his father developed a system for teaching deaf people to speak.
他的母亲逐渐失去了听力，父亲则发明了一套教聋人说话的方法。
After moving to North America, Bell himself became a teacher of deaf students in Boston.
移居北美后，贝尔本人在波士顿成了一名聋人学生的老师。
His knowledge of how sound travels led him to wonder whether a voice could be sent along an electric wire.
他对声音传播方式的了解，促使他思考人声能否沿着电线传送。
He received a patent for the telephone in March 1876, just ahead of other inventors working on similar ideas.
1876年3月，他获得了电话的专利，仅仅领先于其他研究类似构想的发明家。
A few days later, he spoke into his device and his assistant, Thomas Watson, heard from another room: "Mr. Watson, come here — I want to see you."
几天后，他对着装置说话，他的助手托马斯·华生在另一个房间听到：“华生先生，请过来，我想见你。”
Within a few decades, telephone lines connected cities across the continent.
短短几十年间，电话线就连通了整个大陆的城市。
Bell, however, always considered his work with deaf people at least as important as his famous invention.
然而，贝尔始终认为，他为聋人所做的工作至少和他那项著名的发明同样重要。
q: What was Bell's job in Boston?
What were the first words Watson heard through the telephone, according to the article?
"Mr. Watson, come here — I want to see you."
What did Bell think about his work with deaf people?
It was at least as important as the telephone
It was a waste of time
It was less important than his patent

title: Thunder of Waters
p: Niagara Falls sits on the border between the United States and Canada, where the Niagara River drops on its way from Lake Erie to Lake Ontario.
尼亚加拉瀑布位于美国和加拿大的边境，尼亚加拉河从伊利湖流向安大略湖，在这里跌落而下。
It is actually three waterfalls: the Horseshoe Falls, the American Falls and the smaller Bridal Veil Falls.
它实际上由三座瀑布组成：马蹄瀑布、美国瀑布和较小的新娘面纱瀑布。
The largest, the Horseshoe Falls, is shaped like a giant curve and lies mostly on the Canadian side.
其中最大的马蹄瀑布形如一道巨大的弧线，大部分位于加拿大一侧。
Since the 1840s, boats have carried visitors in raincoats close to the base of the falls, where the roar is deafening and the spray soaks everyone.
从19世纪40年代起，就有船只载着身穿雨衣的游客驶近瀑布底部，那里水声震耳欲聋，水雾会把每个人都淋透。
In 1901, a 63-year-old schoolteacher named Annie Edson Taylor became the first person to go over the falls in a barrel and survive.
1901年，一位名叫安妮·埃德森·泰勒的63岁教师成为第一个坐在木桶里冲下瀑布并生还的人。
Much of the river's water is now diverted to power plants that produce electricity for both countries.
如今，大部分河水被引向发电厂，为两国发电。
Under an agreement between the two nations, more water is allowed to flow over the falls during the day, when tourists are watching, than at night.
根据两国之间的协议，白天游客观赏时允许流过瀑布的水量比夜间更多。
q: How many waterfalls make up Niagara Falls?
What did Annie Edson Taylor do in 1901?
She went over the falls in a barrel and survived
She built the first tour boat
She opened the first power plant
Why does less water flow over the falls at night?
More is diverted to produce electricity
Boats need calm water at night
The lakes are lower at night

title: The Return of the Bald Eagle
p: The bald eagle has been the national bird of the United States since 1782, when it was placed on the country's official seal.
自1782年被放上国家国徽起，白头海雕就一直是美国的国鸟。
Despite its name, it is not bald at all; "bald" comes from an old word meaning white-headed.
尽管名字里有“秃”字，它其实一点也不秃；“bald”来自一个意为“白头”的古词。
Not everyone loved the choice: Benjamin Franklin once wrote that the eagle had "bad moral character" and that the turkey was a more respectable bird.
并不是所有人都喜欢这个选择：本杰明·富兰克林曾写道，这种鹰“品行不端”，火鸡反倒是更值得尊敬的鸟。
By the middle of the twentieth century, the eagle was in serious trouble.
到了20世纪中叶，白头海雕的处境岌岌可危。
A widely used pesticide called DDT built up in the fish that eagles ate, causing them to lay eggs with shells so thin that they broke during nesting.
一种被广泛使用的杀虫剂DDT在白头海雕吃的鱼体内积累，导致它们产下的蛋壳非常薄，在孵化时就会破裂。
In the lower 48 states, only a few hundred nesting pairs remained.
在美国本土48个州，只剩下几百对筑巢的白头海雕。
The United States banned DDT in 1972 and protected the birds and their nests by law.
美国于1972年禁用了DDT，并通过法律保护这种鸟及其巢穴。
The recovery was remarkable, and in 2007 the bald eagle was removed from the endangered species list, a symbol of what conservation can achieve.
它们的恢复非常显著，2007年白头海雕被移出濒危物种名单，成为保护工作成效的象征。
q: What does "bald" in the bird's name originally mean?
How did DDT harm the eagles?
It made their eggshells too thin
It poisoned the trees they nested in
It made them unable to fly
The bald eagle was removed from the endangered list
The eagle became the national bird

title: A Gift from a Stranger
p: In 1829, a British scientist named James Smithson died and left his fortune to the United States, a country he had never visited.
1829年，一位名叫詹姆斯·史密森的英国科学家去世，把自己的财产留给了美国——一个他从未去过的国家。
His will asked for an institution in Washington "for the increase and diffusion of knowledge."
他在遗嘱中要求在华盛顿建立一个机构，“以增进和传播知识”。
Nobody is quite sure why he made this choice, and Congress argued for years about how to use the money before founding the Smithsonian Institution in 1846.
没有人确切知道他为什么做出这个选择，国会为如何使用这笔钱争论了多年，才在1846年创立了史密森学会。
Today the Smithsonian is a family of museums, research centers and a national zoo, many of them lined up along the National Mall.
如今，史密森学会拥有众多博物馆、研究中心和一座国家动物园，其中许多沿着国家广场一字排开。
Its collections are so large that it is nicknamed "the nation's attic."
它的藏品之多，使它得了个“国家阁楼”的外号。
Visitors can see the Wright brothers' 1903 Flyer, the famous blue Hope Diamond and the huge flag that inspired "The Star-Spangled Banner."
游客可以看到莱特兄弟1903年的“飞行者号”、著名的蓝色希望钻石，以及启发了《星条旗之歌》的那面巨大旗帜。
Perhaps the best part is that entry to its museums in Washington is free, so families can return again and again.
也许最棒的是，它在华盛顿的博物馆免费入场，所以家庭可以一次又一次地来参观。
q: What was unusual about James Smithson's gift?
He had never visited the United States
He asked for a museum in London
Why is the Smithsonian called "the nation's attic"?
It is very old and dusty
What is said about entry to its museums in Washington?
It is open only on weekends

title: From the Cavern to the World
zh: 从洞穴俱乐部走向世界
p: In the early 1960s, Liverpool was a gritty port city in northwest England whose docks connected it to sailors, goods and records from across the Atlantic.
20世纪60年代初，利物浦还是英格兰西北部一座粗犷的港口城市，码头把它与来自大西洋彼岸的水手、货物和唱片联系在一起。
In a damp basement venue called the Cavern Club, a local band named the Beatles played hundreds of lunchtime and evening shows, sharpening their sound before crowds packed shoulder to shoulder.
在一个名为“洞穴俱乐部”的潮湿地下室场地里，一支名叫披头士的本地乐队演出了数百场午间和晚间演出，在摩肩接踵的人群面前磨砺自己的音乐。
Their raw energy, catchy harmonies and cheeky humor set them apart from the polished pop of the day.
他们原始的活力、朗朗上口的和声以及俏皮的幽默，使他们有别于当时精雕细琢的流行音乐。
On February 9, 1964, the Beatles appeared on The Ed Sullivan Show in New York, watched by an estimated 73 million Americans.
1964年2月9日，披头士登上了纽约的《艾德·沙利文秀》，估计有7300万美国人收看。
The broadcast opened the door to what became known as the "British Invasion," as groups such as the Rolling Stones and the Kinks followed them onto American charts.
这次播出开启了后来被称为“英国入侵”的浪潮，滚石乐队、奇想乐队等团体紧随其后登上了美国排行榜。
Ironically, many of these bands had learned their craft by imitating American rock and roll and blues, so in a sense they were selling America's own music back to it.
具有讽刺意味的是，这些乐队中有许多是通过模仿美国的摇滚乐和布鲁斯来学艺的，所以在某种意义上，他们是把美国自己的音乐又卖回给了美国。
Today, a rebuilt Cavern Club stands on Mathew Street, close to its original site, and Liverpool's waterfront draws music fans from all over the world.
如今，一座重建的洞穴俱乐部矗立在马修街上，靠近原址，利物浦的滨水区吸引着来自世界各地的乐迷。
q: Where did the Beatles develop their sound in Liverpool?
In a basement venue called the Cavern Club
In a recording studio in London
The success of British bands in America after 1964
A war between Britain and America
A TV show about British history
A rule limiting American records in Britain
Why does the author call the British Invasion ironic?
The bands had learned from American music
The bands were not really British

title: Wandering Lonely as a Cloud
p: England's Lake District, a compact region of mountains, valleys and glacial lakes in Cumbria, has shaped how the English-speaking world thinks about landscape.
英格兰的湖区位于坎布里亚郡，是一片由山峦、山谷和冰川湖泊组成的紧凑区域，它塑造了英语世界对风景的看法。
Much of that influence can be traced to William Wordsworth, who was born on its edge in 1770 and later lived at Dove Cottage in Grasmere.
这种影响很大程度上可以追溯到威廉·华兹华斯，他1770年生于湖区边缘，后来住在格拉斯米尔的鸽舍。
Together with Samuel Taylor Coleridge, Wordsworth published Lyrical Ballads in 1798, a collection that rejected elaborate poetic language in favor of ordinary speech and deep feeling.
1798年，华兹华斯与塞缪尔·泰勒·柯勒律治共同出版了《抒情歌谣集》，这部诗集摒弃了繁复的诗歌语言，转而采用平实的日常语言和深沉的情感。
His famous poem about a host of golden daffodils was inspired by a walk beside Ullswater with his sister Dorothy, whose own journal described the scene first.
他那首描写一大片金色水仙的名诗，灵感来自他与妹妹多萝西在阿尔斯沃特湖畔的一次散步，而多萝西在自己的日记里最先描写了那番景象。
The Romantic poets helped persuade readers that wild, untamed nature was not something to be feared but a source of spiritual renewal.
浪漫主义诗人们帮助读者相信：狂野、未被驯服的自然不是令人畏惧的东西，而是心灵复苏的源泉。
A century later, the children's author Beatrix Potter used income from her books to buy farms in the area, leaving more than 4,000 acres to the National Trust when she died.
一个世纪后，儿童文学作家比阿特丽克斯·波特用卖书的收入在当地购买农场，去世时把4000多英亩土地留给了英国国民信托。
The region became a national park in 1951 and a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2017, recognized as much for its working farms and cultural history as for its scenery.
湖区于1951年成为国家公园，2017年被列入联合国教科文组织世界遗产名录，它获得认可既因为其风景，也同样因为其仍在运作的农场和文化历史。
q: What was new about Lyrical Ballads?
It used ordinary speech instead of elaborate language
It was the first book printed in Cumbria
It was written entirely by Dorothy
It described cities rather than nature
Who first described the daffodil scene in writing?
How did Beatrix Potter help protect the Lake District?
She bought farms and left them to the National Trust
She founded the national park in 1951
She sold her farms to developers

title: The Rock at the Heart of a Continent
p: Rising about 348 meters above the flat red desert of Australia's Northern Territory, Uluru is one of the most recognizable natural landmarks on Earth.
乌鲁鲁从澳大利亚北领地平坦的红色荒漠中拔地而起，高约348米，是地球上最具辨识度的自然地标之一。
The huge sandstone formation appears to change color through the day, glowing deep orange and red as the sun sets.
这块巨大的砂岩似乎在一天中不断变色，日落时会泛出深橙和赤红的光芒。
For the Anangu, the Aboriginal people of the area, Uluru is not merely scenery but a sacred place woven into Tjukurpa, the law and knowledge that govern their relationship with the land.
对于当地的原住民阿南古人来说，乌鲁鲁不仅是风景，更是一处圣地，融入了他们的“Tjukurpa”——支配他们与土地关系的法则和知识。

European explorers named it Ayers Rock in 1873, after a colonial official, but in 1985 the land was formally handed back to its traditional owners, who lease it to the national park they now manage jointly with the government.
1873年，欧洲探险者以一位殖民地官员的名字将其命名为“艾尔斯岩”，但在1985年，这片土地正式归还给传统所有者，他们再把土地租给如今与政府共同管理的国家公园。
For decades, tourists climbed the rock, even though the Anangu asked them not to.
几十年来，尽管阿南古人请求游客不要攀爬，游客们还是爬上了这块巨岩。
The climb was permanently closed in October 2019, a decision that some visitors resented but that many saw as overdue respect for Indigenous culture.
2019年10月，攀岩路线被永久关闭，一些游客对此心怀不满，但许多人认为这是对原住民文化迟来的尊重。
Visitors now walk the base trail instead, where signs explain stories connected to particular caves and rock features, and some sacred sites may not be photographed.
如今游客改走环绕岩石底部的步道，沿途的标牌讲解与特定洞穴和岩石特征相关的故事，有些圣地则不允许拍照。
q: The Anangu law and knowledge about the land
The name of a hiking trail
The land was handed back to its traditional owners
The rock was named Ayers Rock
How did people react to the closing of the climb?
Some resented it, but many saw it as respect

title: The Stone That Spoke Three Languages
p: When the British Museum opened in 1759, it was among the first national public museums in the world, built around the vast collection of the physician Sir Hans Sloane.
大英博物馆1759年开馆时，是世界上最早的国家公共博物馆之一，其基础是医生汉斯·斯隆爵士的大量收藏。
Its founding principle — that the collection should be open to all "studious and curious persons" free of charge — still shapes its identity today.
它的建馆原则——收藏应免费向所有“好学和好奇之人”开放——至今仍塑造着它的特质。
Its most visited object is a dark slab of stone found by French soldiers in Egypt in 1799 and handed to the British under a treaty in 1801.
馆内参观人数最多的展品是一块深色石板，它于1799年被法国士兵在埃及发现，1801年根据一项条约移交给了英国人。
The Rosetta Stone carries the same decree written three times: in hieroglyphs, in a script called Demotic and in ancient Greek.
罗塞塔石碑上用三种文字刻着同一份诏令：象形文字、一种叫作世俗体的文字和古希腊文。
Because scholars could read the Greek, the stone became the key to unlocking hieroglyphs, a puzzle that Jean-François Champollion finally cracked in 1822.
由于学者们能读懂希腊文，这块石碑成了破解象形文字的钥匙，让-弗朗索瓦·商博良最终在1822年解开了这个谜题。
Yet the museum's treasures also raise uncomfortable questions.
然而，博物馆的珍宝也引发了一些令人不安的问题。
Many objects were acquired during the height of the British Empire, and countries including Egypt and Greece have asked for some of them to be returned.
许多藏品是在大英帝国鼎盛时期获得的，埃及和希腊等国已要求归还其中一些文物。
The debate over who should own the world's cultural heritage shows no sign of being settled soon.
关于谁应拥有世界文化遗产的争论，看不出会很快平息的迹象。
